jobs.title: Director of Engineering
jobs.description:
Eleven Recruiting is searching for a Director of Engineering on behalf of a well-established aerospace manufacturer in Los Angeles, CA. This organization manages a broad portfolio of licensed aerospace products and assemblies supporting rotorcraft, commercial, military, and business aviation platforms.

Responsibilities

Lead the technical team in new product capability evaluation, risk identification, and mitigation; interface with licensors to define and maintain design authority.
Support license and product transition processes; coordinate engineering participation to ensure process control and validation.
Supervise creation of build instructions, tool definitions, and test fixtures; oversee configuration management.
Set guidelines and supervise document control.
Provide technical support and RCCA for field returns, in-service issues, production issues, and MRB technical analysis and disposition.
Lead the Change Control Board (CCB) as the engineering representative.
Serve as technical liaison with customers, suppliers, and subcontractors; support customer service and sales on technical matters.
Select, recruit, and develop engineering personnel; mentor and cross-train across functions.
Support FAA PMA approval processes; partner with other departments during audit activities.
Ensure continued airworthiness of all products and systems within the site's scope.
Ensure adherence to company procedures and standards across design, production, and in-service support.
Liaise with design authorities on technical data changes; lead development activities under any delegated design authority.
Ensure subcontracted engineering work complies with all regulatory and company requirements.

Qualifications

Required
B.S. in Electrical, Mechanical, or Aerospace Engineering.
10+ years in aerospace design and/or manufacturing engineering; 5+ years in a supervisory role.
Hands-on experience with AC/DC motors, actuators, hydraulic pumps, valves, electronics, and electro-mechanical assemblies.
Knowledge of materials, outside critical processes, NDT, and precision aerospace component specifications.
Project and configuration management experience.
Strong communicator — clear technical reporting, direct customer and licensor interface.

Preferred
M.S. in Engineering and/or MBA.
FAA PMA experience.
Background in licensed manufacturing, MRO, or inherited/legacy product line environments.
Comfort owning design authority where complete technical pedigree is not available.
Familiarity with AS9100, FAA Part 145, and relevant civil/military airworthiness standards.
Experience interfacing with Type Certificate holders and design authorities.
Rotorcraft and/or fixed-wing platform experience.

jobs.title: Sustaining System Engineering Director
jobs.description:
At Zimmer Biomet, we believe in pushing the boundaries of innovation and driving our mission forward. As a global medical technology leader for nearly 100 years, a patient’s mobility is enhanced by a Zimmer Biomet product or technology every 8 seconds.

As a Zimmer Biomet team member, you will share in our commitment to providing mobility and renewed life to people around the world. To support our talented team, we focus on development opportunities, robust employee resource groups (ERGs), a flexible working environment, location specific competitive total rewards, wellness incentives and a culture of recognition and performance awards. We are committed to creating an environment where every team member feels inspired, invested, cared for, valued, and have a strong sense of belonging.

What You Can Expect

Lead post-510(k) engineering support and product life cycle management for released robotic systems across clinical applications, including service operations, complaint handling, and sustaining engineering activities.

This position is onsite in Austin, Texas.

How You'll Create Impact

Own service and fleet management activities for installed robotic systems, including leadership of Field Service Engineering teams to support system uptime, field performance, and customer issues.
Lead complaint handling activities, including investigation, prioritization, and closure of product complaints while partnering with Quality on CAPA activities and regulatory requirements.
Drive sustaining engineering efforts resulting from field issues and complaint trends, translating post-market feedback into product improvements and corrective actions.
Lead root-cause investigations and coordinate cross-functional teams to resolve hardware, software, and system-level issues identified through field use.
Establish processes for identifying recurring field issues, prioritizing actions, and implementing design or process improvements.
Oversee development and maintenance of service manuals, troubleshooting guides, work instructions, and field service procedures to support effective system maintenance and repair.
Manage service bill of materials and spare parts structures to support field repairs, maintenance activities, change management, and long-term product support.
Partner with Quality, Regulatory, Manufacturing, and Product Development teams to ensure post-market learnings are incorporated into ongoing product improvements.
Develop and track metrics around fleet performance, complaint trends, service responsiveness, and product reliability.

What Makes You Stand Out

Driven and highly motivated individual who wants to shape the future of healthcare; takes initiative to identify challenges and propose solutions.
Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire teams.
Demonstrated ability to lead through influence to drive engagement and focus on critical priorities with cross-functional teams.
Broad knowledge of field service practices and principles.
Broad knowledge and practical experience in project management, personnel development and leadership.
Fundamental knowledge of financial management principles.
Superior communication and presentation skills – both written and oral.
Outstanding interpersonal and organizational skills.

Minimum Requirements: Bachelor's Degree and 8 years of relevant experience, or Associate's Degree and 10 years of relevant experience, or High School Diploma or Equivalent and 12 years of relevant experience
Prior experience in medical device and orthopedic robotics strongly preferred
Prior experience leading technical programs, projects a plus
Demonstrated ability to train, mentor, and lead a diverse team on high skilled individuals
Advanced degree preferred

jobs.description:
About Us

QISG leverages Quanta’s comprehensive resources to deliver collaborative solutions for our partners' energy infrastructure needs. We use in-house talent, expertise and resources to plan, design, engineer, manage, conduct maintenance on and construct projects.

Our turnkey service capabilities provide our customers with efficiency, consistency, attention to detail and safe execution. The QISG team brings together Engineering, Safety, Quality, Material Procurement, QA/QC, Right-of-Way Acquisition, Scheduling, Environmental Planning, Permitting, Title and Land Management expertise that ensure outstanding results for our clients.

About This Role

JOB TITLE:
Director, Engineering

The Director of Engineering for Substation is a senior leadership role responsible for overseeing the planning, design, and implementation of Substation projects. This role involves managing a team of engineers and technical staff, ensuring that projects meet regulatory, safety, and quality standards, and supporting the company's strategic objectives. The Director will collaborate with other departments, stakeholders, and external partners to drive innovation, efficiency, and operational excellence in the company's transmission and substation engineering activities.

What You'll Do

Lead, mentor, and develop a team of engineers and technical professionals.
Establish and maintain a high-performance culture, with a focus on continuous improvement and innovation.
Foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment that values diverse perspectives and talents.
Oversee the planning, design, and execution of transmission and substation projects, ensuring alignment with company goals and regulatory requirements.
Develop project budgets, schedules, and resource plans, and ensure projects are delivered on time and within budget.
Manage risks and resolve issues that may impact project scope, quality, and delivery.
Provide technical guidance and expertise in the design and optimization of transmission and substation systems.
Stay current with industry trends, technologies, and regulatory changes, and integrate best practices into the engineering processes.
Ensure compliance with safety, environmental, and regulatory standards in all engineering activities.
Contribute to the development of the company's strategic plans and objectives, particularly in the areas of transmission and substation infrastructure.
Identify and evaluate new business opportunities, partnerships, and technologies that can enhance the company's competitive position.
Collaborate with other departments, such as Operations, Finance, and Regulatory Affairs, to align engineering initiatives with broader business goals.
Build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including customers, regulators, contractors, and suppliers.
Represent the company at industry forums, conferences, and regulatory meetings, advocating for the company's interests and promoting its capabilities.

What You'll Bring

Minimum of 15 years’ experience in the electric utility industry performing engineering related duties and/or management for high voltage electrical projects.
Bachelor of Science degree (B.S.) or Graduate degree in Electrical Engineering from an ABET accredited university.
P.E. license required.
Proven track record of successfully leading multidisciplinary engineering teams and delivering complex projects on time and within budget.
Strong technical expertise in structural, civil, electrical, or mechanical engineering, with a comprehensive understanding of engineering principles and practices.
Expert knowledge of electric utility engineering and construction standards.
Advanced knowledge of utility industry processes including scheduling, contracts, coordinating and managing all disciplines.
Excellent business acumen and experience managing departmental budgets.
Knowledge of process and procedures for project controls and estimates.
Experience interpreting internal and external business issues, recommending best practices, mitigating risk and solving complex problems.
Demonstrated experience supporting external customers.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and leadership skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with internal teams, clients, and external partners.
Demonstrated ability to develop and execute strategic plans, drive innovation, and achieve business objectives.
Knowledge of relevant industry codes, standards, and regulations, including ANSI, ASTM, ACI, AISC, NEC, NESC, and others.
Able to deal with ambiguity and ability to work independently, manage multiple tasks and determine priorities in a complex environment.

jobs.description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world. If you're energized by leading world-class engineering teams, solving hard manufacturing problems, and seeing your work ship at global scale — this might be exactly what you've been looking for!

As Director of Production Test Operations, you'll lead the teams and strategies that bring our most innovative Co-Packaged Optics and Networking chip products from development into production. We need someone who can understand the mission, build team capability, and drive quality execution across US domestic and APAC OSAT sites.

What You Will Be Doing

Lead and develop teams of CPO and Networking Chip Equipment and Production Test engineers - setting direction, developing talent, and holding a high bar for quality and execution.
Define and lead the test manufacturing strategy, aligning processes and performance metrics with broader business and operational objectives.
Partner closely with technology teams, platform suppliers, hardware vendors, test engineering, and OSAT partners to ensure seamless test readiness and ramp execution.
Drive cross-team problem-solving to support high-volume production and resolve complex operational issues with speed and rigor.
Leverage test data and operational KPIs to identify trends, anticipate risk, lead continuous improvement initiatives and ensure production runs smoothly.
Ensure all test operations meet internal standards, industry requirements, and best practices.

What We Need To See

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field (or equivalent experience); advanced degree preferred
15+ overall years in test operations, including 6+ years leading senior technical teams in global organizations
Hands-on experience with SiPH, CPO platforms, and ATE/CPO hardware
Strong background in OSAT factory operations; direct factory experience preferred
A track record of building and growing high-performing teams in complex manufacturing environments
Clear, data-informed communication and decision-making

jobs.description:
Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

The Role

The Autonomous Factory Systems team builds the software that gives Hadrian's factories the ability to sense, decide, and act autonomously. This includes the core robotics stack — perception, behaviors, planning, collision avoidance, and high-level control — alongside orchestration between robots and manufacturing machines and the hardware abstraction layer that connects our software to the machines on the floor.

You will build and manage a team of engineers focused on the robotics side of this stack. This is a people-first management role: your focus is on hiring, growing, and supporting a strong team, while staying close enough to the technical work to help guide direction and staffing decisions.

What You’ll Do

Own the people leadership of your engineers: hiring, onboarding, mentorship, career growth, and performance.
Build a hiring engine for robotics talent — define the bar, run a strong interview process, and help recruit a top-tier team across perception, planning, behaviors, and control.
Ensure engineers are engaged, growing, and set up to do their best work; regularly assess team health and address issues before they become problems.
Have real input into technical direction and where we invest headcount, in close partnership with the engineers and technical leads who drive architecture and design.
Partner with Hardware, Controls, Product, and Operations to translate business priorities into a sequenced roadmap, and make sure the team is resourced and organized to deliver it.
Continuously improve the team's engineering practices and developer lifecycle: planning, design review, code review, testing, simulation, deployment, on-call, and incident response.

What We’re Looking For

5+ years of engineering management experience leading robotics, autonomy, or other complex technical teams in production.
A genuine passion for people management — you care about your engineers' growth and happiness as much as you care about what the team ships.
A track record of hiring and building strong technical teams, including for hard-to-fill or specialized roles.
Technical fluency in robotics concepts (perception, planning, behaviors, control, collision avoidance) to have informed conversations about tradeoffs, evaluate technical leads' proposals, and contribute a useful point of view on direction and prioritization — without needing to be the architect yourself.
Strong judgment on organizational design: how to structure a team, allocate headcount across projects, and balance depth vs. breadth as the stack grows.
Excellent communication and cross-functional partnership skills — you can align engineers, technical leads, hardware/controls partners, and leadership.
A track record of running a healthy team: clear expectations, direct feedback, and a strong sense of ownership among your engineers.
Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment with high stakes, physical systems, and short iteration cycles.
M.S. in Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field.

What Will Set You Apart

A track record of scaling a team through a period of fast headcount growth, including building out interview loops and onboarding from scratch.
Experience mentoring engineers to grow into broader technical leadership roles.
Experience managing engineers across multiple robotics disciplines (e.g., perception and planning)

$299,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

About Safe-guard Products International

Safe-Guard Products International is the industry leader in automotive protection products and F&I solutions, partnering with the world's top OEM brands and a nationwide network of franchised and independent dealerships. Our platforms power the full lifecycle of vehicle protection—from dealer enrollment and incentive management to real-time rating, quoting, contracting, claims adjudication, cancellations, and consumer-direct experiences. We are transforming into an AI-first future culture, embedding intelligence across every platform our dealers, OEM partners, and internal operations teams rely on daily.

As we accelerate AI transformation, we are seeking a proven Head of Software Engineering to lead the engineering organization responsible for our client-facing and internal operations platforms. This is a career-defining opportunity for a technology leader who has built AI-native engineering cultures, delivered AI-powered platforms in complex regulated industries, and knows how to win in both the automotive and insurance environments.

Role Overview

The Head of Software Engineering owns software engineering strategy and execution across Safe-Guard's core platform portfolio. You will lead a multi-team engineering organization that builds and operates the systems underpinning dealer enrollment, incentive programs, rating, quoting, and remitting workflows, claims adjudication, cancellations, payment processing, and direct-to-consumer product experiences. You will partner with Sales, Key Partner Management, Operations, and executive leadership to align engineering capacity and roadmaps with company strategy, and you will help champion Safe-Guard's vision of AI-native software development, operationalizing the use of Claude, Cursor, and similar LLMs and software tools across engineering teams.

Note : This role does not have responsibility for ERP / Financial Systems or Business Analytics / BI reporting platforms.

What You Will Do

Engineering Leadership & Team Development

Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing software engineering organization across multiple product domains, client-facing dealer and OEM platforms, internal operations systems, and direct-to-consumer applications.
Own recruiting, hiring, and retention of top engineering talent; build career progression that reward technical excellence and leadership growth at every level.
Establish and sustain a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous learning for engineers do their best work.
Conduct regular 1:1s, performance reviews, and career development conversations; actively develop direct reports into future leaders.
Partner with HR and Talent Acquisition to strengthen Safe-Guard's employer brand within the software engineering community.

Platform Ownership & Technical Strategy

Own the engineering roadmap and outcomes for Safe-Guard's client-facing platforms (dealer enrollment, rating, quoting, contract remittance, incentive management, direct-to-consumer) and internal platforms (claims adjudication, cancellations, and payments).
Define and help drive the technical architecture strategy, balancing modernization, and scalability, across a portfolio of applications serving automotive and insurance workflows.
Partner with Sales, Product Management, and Operations to translate business objectives into executable technical roadmaps, ensuring alignment between engineering capacity and company priorities.
Drive continuous improvement in system reliability, performance, and security; establish engineering standards for code quality, testing, observability, and incident response.
Make sound architectural and build/buy/partner decisions, clearly communicating trade-offs to senior leadership and stakeholders.

AI-Native Culture & Platform Development

Help champion Safe-Guard's AI vision by embedding AI-assisted development practices as standard practice across all engineering teams.
In collaboration with technology leadership, help design and delivery of AI-native platform capabilities, including intelligent automation in claims adjudication, contract processing, rating workflows, and dealer-facing experiences.
Build a team culture where engineers default to AI-first thinking: leveraging AI to accelerate development velocity, improve code quality, reduce operational work, and expand product capabilities.
Stay current on AI tooling and agentic AI approaches; bring informed recommendations to the technology and product leadership on emerging capabilities applicable to Safe-Guard's platforms.
Establish evaluation frameworks and responsible-use guidelines ensuring AI capabilities deployed in production meet Safe-Guard's quality, compliance, security, and reliability standards.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement

Serve as the primary engineering voice in executive and cross-functional forums; communicate technical strategy, progress, risks, and trade-offs clearly to both technical and business stakeholders.
Partner with Operations, Compliance, and Legal teams to ensure platforms meet the regulatory requirements of automotive and insurance administration.
Collaborate closely with our dealer network, OEM partners, and Key partner executive teams to incorporate external feedback into the platform roadmap.
Drive alignment across peer technology leaders—Product, Architecture, Data, Security, and IT to deliver cohesive, integrated platform experiences.

Delivery Excellence & Operational Maturity

Own end-to-end software delivery accountability ensuring teams execute with predictability, quality, and a consistent sense of urgency.
Implement and refine delivery practices, release cadences, and engineering health metrics that give leadership clear visibility into team performance and platform health.
Drive operational excellence: runbooks, post-incident reviews, and a culture of proactive reliability over reactive firefighting.
Identify and remove organizational and technical blockers that impede team velocity.

Experience

WHAT YOU WILL BRING

15+ years of progressive software engineering experience, including 7+ years leading engineering organizations of 70 or more engineers across multiple teams and domains including offshore contracting resources.
Demonstrated success building and scaling AI-native engineering cultures to fundamentally transform how engineering teams design and build software.
Hands-on experience building AI-powered production platforms; familiarity with LLMs, agentic AI architectures, and practical integration patterns for regulated business workflows.
Direct experience with AI-assisted development tooling including Anthropic's Claude, Cursor, and similar LLMs and products at team or organizational scale.
Proven track record in the automotive industry with direct experience working with dealer networks, OEM brands, or automotive F&I platforms strongly preferred.
Meaningful experience in insurance or insurance-adjacent domains (policy administration, claims processing, coverage rating and quoting, or similar regulated workflows).
Track record delivering complex, client-facing SaaS or platform products in a B2B environment where uptime, performance, and compliance are non-negotiable.

Technical & Domain Expertise

Strong command of modern software architecture patterns: microservices, event-driven systems, API-first design, cloud-native infrastructure, and DevSecOps practices.
Deep familiarity with the software development lifecycle: code quality standards, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, release management, and production observability.
Understanding of the regulatory and compliance landscape relevant to automotive protection products, vehicle service contracts, and insurance product administration.
Experience with payment processing platforms, financial transaction workflows, or claims administration systems is a strong advantage.

Leadership & Communication

Exceptional ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, actionable narratives for executive, business, and cross-functional audiences.
Proven ability to build trust with internal and external customers operating as a credible technology partner, not just an internal function.
High emotional intelligence; skilled at navigating organizational complexity, building consensus across competing priorities, and leading through change.
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field required; advanced degree a plus. Equivalent experience will be considered.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 90 days, you will have built strong relationships with your engineering leads, Product partners, and key business stakeholders; completed a candid assessment of platform health, team capabilities, and delivery practices; and established your presence as a trusted, decisive leader within the Technology organization. Within 6-months, your teams will be operating with measurably improved delivery predictability, AI-assisted development will be embedded in daily engineering workflows, and you will have a clear roadmap for elevating AI-native capabilities across Safe-Guard's platform portfolio. At one year, Safe-Guard's engineering organization will reflect your leadership: higher engineering velocity, a stronger talent bench, AI-powered platform capabilities in production, and an engineering culture where the best people want to stay and grow.

Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

As a Senior Engineering Manager, Communications, you'll lead the team responsible for in-game text chat — one of the most-used surfaces on Roblox and a cornerstone of how our community connects. Every day this system carries billions of messages across hundreds of millions of users, in real time, across 2D and 3D spaces, on every device we support. You'll own the roadmap and the engineering org behind it: building rich, immersive, and engaging communication experiences that let people and creators express themselves safely and seamlessly — better than in real life.

This is a role for a leader who thinks like a product builder as much as an engineer. You'll balance the demands of massive scale and rock-solid reliability with a relentless focus on the user experience, shipping features that make conversation on Roblox feel effortless, expressive, and safe. You'll grow and develop a team of engineers, set technical direction, and partner deeply across product, design, trust & safety, and infrastructure to define what communication on Roblox becomes next.

You Will

Lead, grow, and develop a team of software engineers building the in-game text chat platform, setting a high bar for engineering excellence, ownership, and career growth.
Own the technical vision and multi-quarter roadmap for real-time text messaging, balancing new product capabilities against scale, latency, reliability, and cost.
Drive the architecture and evolution of messaging systems that reliably deliver billions of messages per day at low latency to a global, cross-platform audience.
Partner with product and design to shape a compelling communication experience — treating chat as a product, not just infrastructure — and translate ambiguous goals into concrete plans and shipped features.
Collaborate closely with Trust & Safety, Policy, and ML teams to ensure every messaging experience is safe and civil by design for a young, global user base.
Establish strong engineering practices around quality, observability, on-call health, and operational excellence for systems that must always be available.
Communicate clearly and influence across the organization — with peers, leadership, and cross-functional partners — to align teams behind a shared direction.

You Have

8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years managing and growing engineering teams.

Strong product intuition: you make thoughtful tradeoffs between user experience, technical complexity, and speed, and you care about what you ship, not just how it's built.
Deep experience designing and operating large-scale distributed systems, with a strong grasp of reliability, latency, and the realities of running high-throughput services in production.
Demonstrated ability to attract, develop, and retain strong engineers, and to build healthy, high-performing teams.
Excellent communication and cross-functional leadership skills, with a history of driving alignment across product, design, and engineering.

jobs.title: Director of Software Engineering
jobs.description:
Director, Software Engineering
Position Overview

We are seeking an accomplished Director of Software Engineering
to provide strategic and technical leadership for the development of sophisticated, mission-critical software supporting advanced industrial, manufacturing, and defense-related programs.

This senior leadership role will be responsible for establishing the software engineering vision, shaping technical direction, and overseeing the delivery of secure, dependable, and high-performance software platforms. The Director will work across engineering, product development, systems engineering, manufacturing, quality, cybersecurity, and program management organizations to ensure software capabilities support both current operational requirements and long-term business objectives.

The successful candidate will bring a combination of deep software engineering expertise, organizational leadership, architectural judgment, and experience delivering complex systems in highly regulated or technically demanding environments.

Key Responsibilities
Establish and execute a long-term software engineering strategy aligned with organizational objectives, product roadmaps, and evolving technology requirements.
Provide technical direction across multiple software development programs and ensure consistent engineering practices across teams.
Lead the architecture, design, development, integration, verification, deployment, and sustainment of mission-critical software.
Oversee engineering organizations responsible for embedded, application, platform, systems, and other software technologies as appropriate.
Work closely with product and systems engineering leadership to translate customer and operational requirements into scalable software solutions.
Partner with manufacturing and operations teams to ensure software development activities effectively support production, integration, testing, and lifecycle requirements.
Establish appropriate architectural standards, development methodologies, coding practices, and engineering processes.
Champion modern software development approaches, including automation, continuous integration and delivery, DevSecOps, automated testing, and disciplined configuration management.
Promote appropriate adoption of cloud, data, artificial intelligence, automation, and other emerging technologies where they provide meaningful business or technical value.
Ensure software solutions meet applicable requirements for security, reliability, safety, quality, maintainability, and regulatory compliance.
Collaborate with cybersecurity and information assurance teams to incorporate security throughout the software development lifecycle rather than treating it as a final-stage activity.
Establish engineering metrics and performance indicators to monitor delivery, quality, reliability, technical debt, productivity, and operational effectiveness.
Identify technical risks and organizational constraints and develop strategies to address them before they affect program execution.
Balance near-term delivery commitments with longer-term investments in architecture, infrastructure, tooling, modernization, and engineering capability.
Provide technical guidance during major design reviews, architecture decisions, program planning activities, and critical issue resolution.
Ensure engineering teams maintain appropriate documentation, development standards, test strategies, and configuration controls.
Support the evaluation and introduction of new technologies, tools, platforms, and development methodologies.
Coordinate software development activities across geographically distributed teams and ensure effective collaboration between locations and functions.

Organizational Leadership
A major component of this position is building and developing a strong engineering organization.
The Director will:
Lead and mentor engineering managers and senior technical leaders.
Establish clear organizational structures, responsibilities, objectives, and performance expectations.
Recruit, develop, and retain highly skilled software engineering professionals.
Build succession plans and create opportunities for technical and leadership development.
Foster an environment where engineers are encouraged to challenge assumptions, propose improvements, and take ownership of technical outcomes.
Promote collaboration between software, systems, hardware, manufacturing, product, quality, and cybersecurity organizations.
Develop a culture centered on accountability, engineering excellence, continuous learning, and measurable improvement.
Encourage knowledge sharing and consistency of engineering practices across teams and locations.
Help create an inclusive environment in which diverse technical perspectives contribute to better engineering decisions.

Program & Product Partnership
The Director will serve as a senior software representative in broader product and program discussions. This includes partnering with stakeholders to establish realistic development strategies, prioritize technical investments, and align engineering capacity with business needs.
You will help ensure that software roadmaps remain synchronized with product development, system architecture, manufacturing schedules, customer requirements, and future technology initiatives.

The role will also involve communicating complex technical issues to senior leadership, clearly explaining tradeoffs, risks, resource requirements, and recommended courses of action.

Quality, Safety & Security
Because the software supports high-consequence applications, strong attention to reliability and compliance is essential.

The Director will help ensure that engineering teams:
Apply appropriate software quality and verification practices.
Incorporate cybersecurity principles throughout development and deployment.
Follow applicable safety, regulatory, contractual, and industry requirements.
Maintain rigorous configuration and change-control processes.
Identify and mitigate reliability and security risks.
Establish appropriate automated and manual testing strategies.
Address defects and technical debt systematically.
Maintain traceability between requirements, implementation, verification, and released capabilities.
Continuously improve engineering processes based on lessons learned and measurable performance data.

Strategic Technology Leadership
Beyond day-to-day delivery, this position will help define the organization's future software capabilities.

The Director will evaluate emerging technologies and determine where modernization can improve engineering efficiency, product capability, scalability, security, or competitiveness. This may include evaluating new development frameworks, automation platforms, AI-assisted engineering tools, distributed architectures, advanced simulation environments, data platforms, or other technologies relevant to the organization's products.

The ideal leader will understand that modernization is not simply about adopting new technology; it requires thoughtful architecture, disciplined implementation, effective change management, and measurable business or engineering outcomes.

What We're Looking For
The ideal candidate is a strategic engineering leader who remains technically credible while operating effectively at an organizational level. You should be comfortable moving between high-level strategy and detailed technical discussions and have demonstrated success leading complex software organizations.

Strong candidates will typically bring:
Significant experience leading software engineering organizations.
A strong background in software architecture, development, integration, and delivery.
Experience managing engineering managers and senior technical professionals.
Demonstrated success delivering complex, high-reliability or mission-critical software.
Experience working in environments where security, safety, quality, and regulatory requirements are important.
Strong understanding of modern software engineering practices and development methodologies.
Experience establishing technical strategy and multi-year engineering roadmaps.
Strong program and stakeholder management capabilities.
Excellent written, verbal, and executive communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop, and retain high-performing technical teams.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
The ability to make sound technical decisions while balancing schedule, cost, risk, quality, and long-term maintainability.

Leadership Profile

We are looking for a leader who can combine technical depth with organizational vision
. The successful candidate will be able to establish direction without unnecessarily restricting innovation, create accountability without compromising collaboration, and make difficult engineering decisions while keeping teams focused on mission and customer outcomes.

This is an opportunity to influence the technology strategy of a sophisticated organization, shape the next generation of software capabilities, and build an engineering culture capable of delivering dependable solutions for some of the most technically challenging applications in the industry.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Machine Learning
jobs.description:
About Checkr

Checkr is building the data platform to power safe and fair decisions. Over 140,000 companies and millions of people rely on Checkr for AI verification in the moments that matter most: getting a new job, a new place to live, a car ride, childcare, even a date. Customers include Uber, Pennymac, Airbnb, Doordash, and Anthropic.

We’re a team that thrives on solving complex problems with innovative solutions that advance our mission. Checkr is recognized on Forbes Cloud 100 2025 List and is a Y Combinator 2024 Breakthrough Company.

We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to lead the Machine Learning Engineering team inside Checkr’s Data & ML organization. This team sits at the heart of our product's strategic advantage, making millions of background checks faster, more accurate, and more trustworthy.

The Team Owns Three Connected Areas

Core product intelligence: NLP and classification systems, entity resolution, profile integrity, model accuracy, and the production services that power Checkr’s products.
Workforce integrity: resume and identity fraud, multi-signal risk detection, and new products that help customers identify sophisticated hiring fraud
ML and agent infrastructure: evaluation systems, observability, model lifecycle, agent orchestration, and reusable infrastructure that helps every team ship reliable AI faster.

This is an engineering leadership role, not a research-management role: you will lead ML engineers across seniority levels, stay close enough to the work to set technical direction, and hold the team accountable for production outcomes. You will decide where ML should continue to create a strategic advantage for Checkr.

You will also shape Checkr’s broader AI strategy. The near-term agenda includes building a measurable accuracy moat in our core products, launching an end-to-end workforce-integrity product, and creating the evaluation and knowledge infrastructure required to operate AI agents in a regulated domain. This role reports to the Sr. Director of Data & ML within Engineering. This role is based in San Francisco. We are looking for someone who is seeking less process and more shipping, less paperwork and more results.

What You’ll Do

Lead and grow the ML Engineering team. Hire, coach, and develop ML engineers. Set clear ownership, grow technical leaders, and build a team that generates its own roadmap.
Set the strategy and roadmap. Turn ambiguous company priorities into a focused, multi-quarter ML agenda. Put investment on work that improves customer outcomes, revenue, accuracy, reliability, or cost. Stop work that does not.
Raise the production engineering bar. Models and agents ship as dependable software: clear APIs, tests, CI/CD, observability, on-call ownership, and defined reliability targets.
Build the ML operating model. Establish shared approaches to evaluation, golden sets, training-data provenance, model and prompt versioning, monitoring, retraining, latency, and cost. Replace artisanal evaluation with repeatable systems.
Advance core product intelligence. Guide systems for classification, information extraction, entity resolution, profile integrity, and accuracy. Make model quality measurable in production and drive the feedback loops that improve it.
Launch new AI and fraud products. Partner with Product, Security, Operations, and go-to-market teams to turn signals across identity, resume, device, and employment data into customer products.
Lead Checkr’s agentic transition. Guide the design of AI systems that combine specialized models, LLMs, tools, and governed knowledge.
Operate as an executive partner. Explain technical choices and risks in plain language. Align Product Engineering, Product, Operations, Legal, Security, and company leadership when incentives or constraints conflict.
Model AI-native leadership. Use AI to increase the team’s speed and ambition. Keep ownership of every output. As generated code becomes cheaper, raise the bar on judgment, verification, and system design.

What You Bring

10+ years building software and machine learning or AI systems, with a clear progression in scope and impact.
3+ years managing ML or software engineers, including hiring and developing senior and staff-level technical leaders.
A strong software-engineering foundation and a record of shipping ML systems that run in production.
Technical depth across the ML lifecycle: data and labeling, experimentation, model selection, deployment, APIs, CI/CD, observability, evaluation, retraining, and incident response.
Sound judgment across classical ML, deep learning, LLMs, rules, and conventional software.
Experience setting direction for NLP, classification, extraction, entity resolution, risk, fraud, recommendation, or similarly complex applied-ML domains.
Fluency with modern LLM systems, including structured outputs, tool use, agent orchestration, retrieval, evaluation, latency, quality, and cost trade-offs.

jobs.title: Director Engineering - Synthetic Molecule Design and Development
jobs.description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.

At Lilly, Synthetic Molecule Design and Development (SMDD) is involved in key activities for the development of synthetic active pharmaceutical ingredients from pre-clinical phases through commercialization of drug substances and drug products. Our scientists and engineers develop key technical and business solutions across the portfolio using their deep technical expertise to accelerate testing of the clinical hypothesis and overall drug development. SMDD delivers on these responsibilities by recognizing diverse talent and cultures are necessary to bring the next generation of life changing medicines to patients.

Position Summary

Our team is looking for experienced, creative, and energetic candidates to lead unit operation development and process optimization of synthetic drug candidates to support clinical trials, regulatory submission, and product commercialization. The position presents an opportunity to lead dynamic teams comprised of process chemists, analytical chemists, formulation scientists, and engineers.

Responsibilities

Possess fluent knowledge in unit operation design, process modeling, process equipment selection, and scale-up methodologies with a drive to challenge existing methods; create and apply cutting edge technology and novel platforms within a time constrained environment.
Familiarity and working knowledge of modern synthetic organic chemistry.
Demonstrate high learning agility with the ability to understand and exploit new scientific concepts and methods across multiple disciplines; be able to apply these learnings to a portfolio of small molecule, oligonucleotide, and synthetic peptide modalities.
Lead and/or supervise the design and development of new synthetic routes for the manufacture of active pharmaceutical ingredients using the most modern technologies, including continuous processing, automated reaction screening, PAT, and modeling and simulation.
Ability to lead a cross-disciplinary team to evaluate and refine new manufacturing routes, manufacturing technologies, and practices to deliver a challenging portfolio.
Comfortable with scientific uncertainty and the ability to translate hypotheses into action.
Encourage team members to take initiative and accountability to achieve goals; draws out and encourages others to share knowledge.
Provide technical guidance in the scale-up and demonstration of new chemical processes in development and commercial scale equipment. Participate in technology transfer activities to CRO/CMO organizations and Lilly manufacturing to ensure processes are technically sound, well developed and characterized, and safe.
Design laboratory experimentation in support of process design, definition, optimization, and technology transfer objectives. Ability to generate process (and property design) data based on a fundamental understanding of the underlying physical processes. Utilize advancements in technology (PAT) and modeling platforms to understand and direct experimental protocols.
Plan and manage short term and long-term development activities. Develop and/or review technical agendas and timelines for project work. Recommend resource allocation to accomplish projects according to plans, communicate progress and propose changes in timeline, objectives, or direction.
Collaborate with internal and external manufacturing partners to develop robust chemical process that are readily amenable to efficient drug substance manufacturing.
Collaborate closely with Product Delivery, Project Management, Quality, Manufacturing, and Regulatory scientists to execute and deliver material and information for clinical trials and regulatory submissions.
Embrace diverse thought, background, and experience to deliver innovative solutions.
Possess strong communication (oral, written), organizational, and leadership skills.
Supervise, mentor and develop scientific staff. Ensure continued technical and professional growth of group members, encourage efforts towards excellence and knowledge sharing.
Active participant in the external environment and the ability to recognize and apply external innovation and across the Lilly synthetic portfolio.
Possess deep understanding of the external global regulatory climate and emerging requirements. Ability to address key CMC regulatory questions that enable clinical studies and support marketing authorization applications.

Basic Qualifications

Ph.D. in chemical engineering or a closely related field with 8+ years of experience; or MS degree with 15+ years of experience.
Experience developing chemical processes the from mid-development cycle (proof of concept) to product commercialization required
Experience with technical transfer of processes into manufacturing operations required
Experience within the pharmaceutical sector is desired; however, other relevant experience may meet expectations. Prior experience in the development of an active ingredient and associated formulated product is acceptable. Relevant industrial sectors include agrochemicals, nutraceuticals, specialty chemicals, and personal care products.

Additional Skills/Preferences

Experience with authoring regulatory submissions and responding to regulatory questions.
Experience with modeling and simulation tools, data analytics, and predictive analytics.
Experience with online and offline analytical techniques and process analytical technologies (PAT).
Strong technical skills to supply business value.
Creativity and ability to transform ideas into marketable products and processes.
Knowledge and experience with management of a technical project.
Demonstrated leadership capabilities especially in a team environment.
Demonstrated ability to drive and accept change.
Demonstrated success in persuasion, influence and negotiation.
Good interpersonal skills and a sustained tendency for collaboration.
Ability to prioritize multiple activities and manage ambiguity.
Ability to influence others to promote a positive work environment.
Understanding and awareness of the external scientific and regulatory landscape.
Demonstrated initiative and risk-taking.
Demonstrated technical proficiency and ability to create ideas for future work plans.
Established external publication record.

Additional Information

Travel: 0 -10%
Position Local: Indianapolis, IN; Lilly Technology Center-North (LTC-N)

About Us

QISG leverages Quanta’s comprehensive resources to deliver collaborative solutions for our partners' energy infrastructure needs. We use in-house talent, expertise and resources to plan, design, engineer, manage, conduct maintenance on and construct projects.

About This Role

Job Title: Director, Engineering - Transmission Line

At QISG, our Transmission Line teams play a vital role in the safe, reliable, and efficient delivery of power across communities and regions. We design, build, maintain, and upgrade high-voltage transmission infrastructure that supports the backbone of the electric grid. Whether working on new construction, line upgrades, or critical maintenance, our teams ensure projects are executed with the highest standards of safety, quality, and performance. Our work involves both traditional methods and the latest industry innovations to deliver sustainable, cost-effective, and reliable solutions for our customers.

The Director of Engineering for Transmission is a senior leadership role responsible for overseeing the planning, design, and implementation of transmission line projects. This role involves managing a team of engineers and technical staff, ensuring that projects meet regulatory, safety, and quality standards, and supporting the company's strategic objectives. The Director will collaborate with other departments, stakeholders, and external partners to drive innovation, efficiency, and operational excellence in the company's transmission engineering activities.

Lead, mentor, and develop a team of engineers and technical professionals.
Establish and maintain a high-performance culture, with a focus on continuous improvement and innovation.
Foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment that values diverse perspectives and talents.
Oversee the planning, design, and execution of transmission and substation projects, ensuring alignment with company goals and regulatory requirements.
Develop project budgets, schedules, and resource plans, and ensure projects are delivered on time and within budget.
Manage risks and resolve issues that may impact project scope, quality, and delivery.
Provide technical guidance and expertise in the design and optimization of transmission and substation systems.
Stay current with industry trends, technologies, and regulatory changes, and integrate best practices into the engineering processes.
Ensure compliance with safety, environmental, and regulatory standards in all engineering activities.
Contribute to the development of the company's strategic plans and objectives, particularly in the areas of transmission and substation infrastructure.
Identify and evaluate new business opportunities, partnerships, and technologies that can enhance the company's competitive position.
Collaborate with other departments, such as Operations, Finance, and Regulatory Affairs, to align engineering initiatives with broader business goals.
Build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including customers, regulators, contractors, and suppliers.
Represent the company at industry forums, conferences, and regulatory meetings, advocating for the company's interests and promoting its capabilities.
Other duties as assigned

Minimum of 15 years’ experience in the electric utility industry performing engineering related duties and/or management for high voltage electrical projects.
Bachelor of Science degree (B.S.) or Graduate degree in Engineering from an ABET accredited university.
P.E. license required.
Proven track record of successfully leading multidisciplinary engineering teams and delivering complex projects on time and within budget.
Strong technical expertise in structural, civil, electrical, or mechanical engineering, with a comprehensive understanding of engineering principles and practices.
Expert knowledge of electric utility engineering and construction standards.
Advanced knowledge of utility industry processes including scheduling, contracts, coordinating and managing all disciplines.
Excellent business acumen and experience managing departmental budgets.
Knowledge of process and procedures for project controls and estimates.
Experience interpreting internal and external business issues, recommending best practices, mitigating risk and solving complex problems.
Demonstrated experience supporting external customers.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and leadership skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with internal teams, clients, and external partners.
Demonstrated ability to develop and execute strategic plans, drive innovation, and achieve business objectives.
Knowledge of relevant industry codes, standards, and regulations, including ANSI, ASTM, ACI, AISC, NEC, NESC, and others.
Able to deal with ambiguity and ability to work independently, manage multiple tasks and determine priorities in a complex environment.

Veolia in North America is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country's largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. Veolia helps commercial, industrial, healthcare, higher education and municipality customers throughout North America. Headquartered in Boston, Veolia has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across North America.

Job Description

Position Purpose:

This position is responsible for directing all activities related to the management of the Mid-Atlantic Engineering Department for the successful delivery of the overall capital plan for the region. Projects will include Water and Wastewater Projects, including water treatment upgrades, pump stations, storage tanks, pipelines, and other facilities, and wastewater upgrades related to wastewater plants, lift stations and the collection system.

The candidate works closely with Engineering and Operations personnel, managing and coordinating program activities utilizing a cross functional team approach.

The candidate works with a variety of internal and external stakeholders to ensure the capital plan is developed and delivered to meet the system needs, while working with Regulators on compliance and rate filing activities, and being part of a Team to implement the Company's strategic growth plan.

Accountable for delivery of $50M+ of water/wastewater projects annually, including conceptual design/development, coordination of pilot testing, development of the project plans and project delivery through closeout.
Responsible for hiring, supervising, managing, mentoring the Engineering Team.
Works closely with the rate department to develop capital plans and testimony for rate filings as well as testifying before rate commissions as needed.
Support or lead business development efforts and participate in external professional activities that enhance Veolia's standing with state, regional, and national environmental and economic regulators.
Ensure corporate Technical and Environmental Health and Safety/Security standards are incorporated into the design specifications of projects.
Manage environmental and governmental permitting in coordination with local business unit staff.
Support the oversight of construction management personnel to ensure timely completion of assignments, budget compliance and adherence to applicable standards.
Drive efficiency into project delivery through the monitoring of delivery metrics and utilization of alternate procurement and delivery methods.
Provide monthly reports to management regarding the status of capital projects and issues affecting project performance.
Participate in the development of engineering design and delivery processes and standards.
Provide technical expertise on engineering and operational issues and support facility condition assessments for water/wastewater operations.
Ability to work transversally with corporate and local business units.

Work Environment

Successful candidates must be willing to travel to the various business unit sites as per job requirements.
Job sites generally located within a 30-mile radius of the local office with the occasional requirement for sites that are a longer distance.
The Director of Engineering for the Mid-Atlantic region will be based in either Wilmington, DE or Harrisburg, PA, with regular presence required at both office locations.

Bachelor's Degree in Civil, Mechanical or Environmental Engineering.
Minimum 15 years of experience managing water/wastewater design and construction projects and upgrade projects for treatment plants, pumping stations, wastewater collection systems and water transmission/distribution systems.
5+ year Experience leading and managing multi-faceted teams.
Experience utilizing alternate project delivery methods (design-build, integrated project delivery) and contracting methods (guaranteed maximum price, reimbursable).

Thorough working knowledge of water and wastewater processes and system development.
Superior personal effectiveness skills, visible "leadership by example" utilizing participative management involving employees and teamwork whenever possible.
Strong project management skills (initiating, planning, executing, monitoring, controlling and closing).
Strong communication, presentation and reporting skills.
Computer skills (MS Project, Google Suite, Oracle PeopleSoft, Oracle Hyperion or other planning/performance/budgeting tools a plus).
Financial analysis skills, including budget management, ongoing assessment of project risks/opportunities and basic accounting knowledge.

jobs.description:
TITLE: SR. MANAGER, EQUIPMENT ENGINEERING

FLSA: EXEMPT

REPORTS TO: DIRECTOR, EQUIPMENT ENGINEERING AND MAINTENANCE

SUMMARY:

Under the direction of the of Director of Equipment Engineering and Maintenance, the Sr. Manager of Equipment Engineering is responsible for leading a team of highly-skilled equipment engineers in a fast paced thin-film manufacturing environment. Additional responsibilities include in-depth hardware or software trouble-shooting, modification, upgrade, evaluation, selection, ordering, and installation of a wide-range of toolsets used in the wafer fab manufacturing process; analyzing data, compiling reports, presenting findings, and recommending corrective action if required; manages projects of various size, scope, and budget; consistently seeks opportunities to optimize tool performance, increase yield, and lower overall operational costs. This position is located in Milpitas, California.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Manages, develops, and evaluates personnel to ensure the efficient operation of the department; makes employment-related decisions as necessary including hiring and terminations
Develops and maintains tool standards and procedures and ensures equipment engineers are adhering to them consistently
Coordinates tool data analysis, compiles reports, presents findings, recommends corrective action, and proposes long-term improvement plan if needed
Tracks installation, site acceptance testing, and mass production readiness of new equipment. Oversees the relocation of existing equipment in order to optimize workflow
Develops, implements, and maintains a system to track tool records, inspections, warrantees, and service agreements
Collaborates with manufacturing engineering or other cross functional teams to identify and resolve repetitive equipment issues, improve equipment reliability, review procedures, preventative maintenance (PM) frequency, and minimize equipment downtime
Monitors critical tool performance and ensures the tools are maintained per the established schedule and meet specification
Investigates and implements countermeasures to prevent pre-mature part breakdown
Uses AutoCAD, SolidWorks, or similar software to review and verify diagrams or schematics
Responds to inquiries for engineering support from other departments or groups. Prioritizes projects and assists with allocating engineering resources when additional maintenance is required during critical tool down event
Researches, develops, and implements an emergency tool recovery plan to ensure tools remain functional during hard down situations
Adheres to all safety policies and procedures as required
Performs other duties of a similar nature or level*

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor’s degree in Electronics, Mechanical Engineering, and/or equivalent relevant experience
Ten years of experience working as an Sr. Equipment Engineer in a high volume manufacturing environment in the semiconductor industry
Five years of experience in a leadership role
Experience using AutoCAD, SolidWorks, or similar software program
Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office Applications

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

Must have strong collaboration skills to inspire good teamwork among colleagues and vendor counterparts
Knowledge and ability to research, evaluate, order, install, maintain, or upgrade various types of equipment, tools, or tool sets
Knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing principles, practices, and techniques as they relate to equipment engineering and maintenance
Must have sound troubleshooting skills and fluency to work on equipment-related issues
Knowledge and ability to use Microsoft Office applications to create spreadsheets, Word documents, and presentations
Knowledge and ability to use AutoCAD, SolidWorks, or similar software program to review and verify schematics or drawings
Able to manage multiple equipment projects of various scope, schedule, and budget successfully
Able to implement procedures which increase reliability, lower cost, and improve tool performance
Able to analyze data, compile reports, and recommend corrective action
Able to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with all levels of contractors, consultants, employees, and management
Able to work productively and collaboratively with all levels of employees and management
Able to comply with all safety policies and procedures
Demonstrated organizational and time management skills
Demonstrated problem-solving and trouble-shooting skills
Flexible and able to prioritize

The annual base salary for this full-time position is between $145,407.00-$210,000.00 + bonus target + benefits. Within the range the individual pay may differ depending on additional factors including job responsibilities, job related knowledge, skills, abilities, education, and experience. The annual base pay range shown is subject to change and may be modified periodically.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

The Sr. Manager of Equipment Engineering works primarily in an indoor environment from Monday thru Friday. The schedule may be altered from time-to-time to meet business or operational needs; may travel from building-to-building as needed. Works in a class 100 ESD sensitive wafer manufacturing facility; wears a cleanroom (bunny) suit, including hood, gloves, safety glasses, booties, and mask. May be exposed to hazardous conditions, chemicals, fumes, and/or gases during the course of work day; may be exposed to loud noise. Stands and walks, bends, twists, and crawls; May occasionally be required to work in crawl spaces, shafts, or other areas that could cause claustrophobia. Performs various fine grasping movements; operates a computer and enters information using a keyboard, operates a telephone, and other office equipment; may occasionally be required to push, pull, or lift up to 30 pounds.

*Other duties of a similar nature or level are duties that may be required, but may not be specifically listed in the job description or posting.

About This Role

Job Title: Director, Engineering - Transmission Line

At QISG, our Transmission Line teams play a vital role in the safe, reliable, and efficient delivery of power across communities and regions. We design, build, maintain, and upgrade high-voltage transmission infrastructure that supports the backbone of the electric grid. Whether working on new construction, line upgrades, or critical maintenance, our teams ensure projects are executed with the highest standards of safety, quality, and performance. Our work involves both traditional methods and the latest industry innovations to deliver sustainable, cost-effective, and reliable solutions for our customers.

The Director of Engineering for Transmission is a senior leadership role responsible for overseeing the planning, design, and implementation of transmission line projects. This role involves managing a team of engineers and technical staff, ensuring that projects meet regulatory, safety, and quality standards, and supporting the company's strategic objectives. The Director will collaborate with other departments, stakeholders, and external partners to drive innovation, efficiency, and operational excellence in the company's transmission engineering activities.

Develop project budgets, schedules, and resource plans, and ensure projects are delivered on time and within budget.
Manage risks and resolve issues that may impact project scope, quality, and delivery.
Provide technical guidance and expertise in the design and optimization of transmission and substation systems.
Stay current with industry trends, technologies, and regulatory changes, and integrate best practices into the engineering processes.
Ensure compliance with safety, environmental, and regulatory standards in all engineering activities.

Identify and evaluate new business opportunities, partnerships, and technologies that can enhance the company's competitive position.
Collaborate with other departments, such as Operations, Finance, and Regulatory Affairs, to align engineering initiatives with broader business goals.
