jobs.title: Assistant Vice President, Infrastructure
jobs.description:
The University at Buffalo
(UB) invites nominations and applications for the position of Assistant Vice President of Infrastructure (AVP). Reporting to the Vice President and Chief Information Officer, the AVP will be responsible for leading the Enterprise Infrastructure Services and Network and Communication Services units across UB's three campuses.

University at Buffalo

Impactful research
,scholarly distinction, transformative student experiences, and far-reaching service to local, state, national, and international communities define UB's mission as one of the nation's leading public research universities. UB was founded in 1846 as a private medical college located in downtown Buffalo and joined the SUNY network in 1962. SUNY is the largest state university system in the United States, and UB is a flagship campus and the largest and most comprehensive public research university within the system. In 1989, UB was among the first public universities in the Northeast to be admitted into the AAU. Over the years, UB's scope and mission have expanded significantly as it has grown into a world-renowned research university that is the thriving heart of the regional community, a national leader in public higher education, and a global hub for excellence in research and education.

UB enrolls more than 32,000 students (approximately two-thirds undergraduate and one-third graduate and professional students) and offers more than 500 degree programs at the baccalaureate, master's, professional, and doctoral levels acrossits 12 decanal units
. UB has a distinguished faculty of over 1,500 full-time members. UB is currently undertaking its largest faculty­ hiring initiative in recent history, Advancing Top 25: UB Faculty Hiring
, with plans to recruit upward of 200 full-time faculty over the next two years.

UB is home to more than 120 research centers and institutes; its current annual research expenditures, including those in affiliated institutions, exceed $425 million. UB's academic programs and facilities are located on three distinct campuses in the Buffalo metropolitan area. UB's North Campus, located in the suburb of Amherst, is the university's main undergraduate campus and home to the university's primary athletics and cultural facilities. Three miles to the south, on the northern edge of the City of Buffalo, is the university's historic South Campus, home to many of the university's professional schools. The focal point of UB's third, downtown campus center is the Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus, on which UB's state-of-the-art Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences is in proximity to the university's health and life science partners. UB also competes in the prestigious Mid-American Conference and at the highest level of National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) competition, the FBS Division I level.

With an annual operating revenue of $850 million, UB and its affiliated entities generate an estimated economic impact of $2.1 billion annually in New York State. The university's total workforce of over 9,000 full-time equivalent employees makes it one of the region's largest employers. UB is also a leader and an active partner with the more than 20 public and private colleges and universities in the Buffalo-Niagara region.

The Position

The Assistant Vice President for Infrastructure (AVP)
is a dynamic and visionary leader that is a strategic partner and advisor to the Vice President and Chief Information Officer (VPCIO)
. This is a VPCIO Cabinet Leadership
position that plays a pivotal role in shaping and growing the UB Information Technology (UBIT)
organization to align with and advance the university's goals. As a member of the VPCIO Cabinet, the AVP will ensure that UBIT’s people, processes, and technology are equipped to support the university's mission. The AVP directs special projects and strategic priorities as assigned by the VPCIO, spanning institutional planning, cross-divisional partnerships, and IT governance. This position serves as a senior thought leader in the university’s digital transformation efforts, proactively contributing towards the future direction of technology at the university.

The AVP for Infrastructure
provides strategic leadership for the Enterprise Infrastructure Services (EIS
) and Network and Communication Services (NCS)
units, ensuring UB’s network, cloud, data center, and core computer environments remain secure, reliable, and scalable, while advancing technologies, systems, and processes to meet UB’s goals. Working closely with campus partners and IT leadership, the AVP drives coordinated service delivery, continuous improvement, and infrastructure innovation that supports the university’s academic, research, and administrative needs.

This is a newly created role, and the AVP
will have the opportunity to shape how these two units – each with its own history, culture, and operating rhythm – come together as a single, unified infrastructure organization. The successful candidate will build trust across both teams while also thinking beyond day-to-day operations: reassessing UB’s data center footprint, advancing a deliberate cloud and colocation strategy, and positioning the university’s infrastructure to support an ambitious research and AI agenda. The AVP
will need to balance the discipline required to keep mission-critical systems running with the vision to challenge long-standing practices and move UBIT’s infrastructure into closer alignment with where the university is headed.

Key Responsibilities

Departmental Leadership

Provide strategic direction and oversight to the EIS and NCS units, which includes establishing and advancing a cohesive portfolio strategy aligned with the university’s mission and goals and VPCIO priorities, ensuring coordination across infrastructure and communication systems, emerging technologies, and customer-facing services
This role carries a substantive policymaking function. By directing the planning, design, and operation of the university’s data networks, telecommunications, and enterprise infrastructure systems, the AVP leads the establishment and enforcement of the technical and operational policies that guide campus wide technology use, reliability, security, and compliance. The position’s regular engagement with senior academic and administrative leadership ensures that infrastructure standards and related policies align with institutional priorities.
Lead long-range and annual planning, including workforce and succession planning, budget oversight, and investment prioritization to ensure sustainable operations and future-ready capabilities
Assess the current structure, staffing levels, and operations of EIS and NCS, and lead the organizational changes needed to address staffing gaps, evolving service demands, and succession needs, given the significant portion of both units’ workforce eligible for retirement in the coming years
Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement by promoting professional development, mentoring leaders, and enabling teams to deliver high-quality, secure, and customer-centered IT solutions

Drive Strategic Alignment

Ensure that IT initiatives are closely aligned with the university’s strategic goals and mission
Work with university leadership to shape, prioritize, and execute projects that support academic, administrative, and research objectives, while balancing divisional advocacy with institutional priorities and shared enterprise outcomes

Foster Synergies

Promote collaboration and synergy among UBIT departments including but not limited to Innovation, Enterprise Application Services, IT Customer Experience, and Research IT
Leverage strengths and expertise to create a cohesive, efficient IT environment that enhances performance and innovation

Innovate and Transform

Champion innovation and transformation and identify opportunities for technological advancements, process improvements, and new initiatives that move the university forward
Lead the evaluation and evolution of UB’s data center strategy, including assessment of colocation options and consolidation of aging, decentralized data center and server infrastructure across campus
Advance UB’s cloud adoption strategy, building on early planning efforts to shift appropriate administrative and enterprise systems to cloud and hybrid-cloud environments
Partner with UBIT’s Innovation and Research IT units, and academic and research partners to ensure infrastructure supports the university’s growing AI and research computing needs
Champion improvements in customer service and responsiveness across EIS and NCS, working to change perceptions of infrastructure as a barrier to progress and building stronger partnerships with academic and administrative units

Build and Strengthen UBIT

In partnership with other AVPs and senior leaders within UBIT, build and strengthen the VPCIO organization in operating as an integrated leadership team
Develop and implement strategies to enhance the capabilities and effectiveness of UBIT while fostering a culture of continuous improvement, and ensuring that the VPCIO is well-positioned to support the university's evolving needs

Buffalo Niagara

As a world-renowned research university, UB's intellectual capital and innovation are playing a vital role in Buffalo's resurgence as a thriving city that is a magnet for talented professionals, artists, entrepreneurs, and innovators who recognize the tremendous energy and momentum gathering here. Home to one of the nation's fastest growing populations of college graduates, the Buffalo­Niagara region, with 1.2 million residents, is the state's second largest major metropolitan area, exceeded only by New York City. The region includes a diverse blend of communities, each with its own distinct personality, yet commonly characterized by a distinctly neighborly way of life, an unpretentious nature and spirited loyalty among residents. Buffalo's own strong sense of community, easy lifestyle, and affordability regularly place it in top ten lists from a variety of national publications for its overall quality of life.

Rich in natural resources and beauty, the Buffalo-Niagara area is a four-season region that offers the best for seasonal sports enthusiasts. University at Buffalo fans enjoy a full complement of NCAA division I sports with the UB Bulls, as well as the NFL's Buffalo Bills, the NH L's Buffalo Sabres, Triple­A baseball's Buffalo Bisons, and the National Lacrosse League's Buffalo Bandits.

Less than a two-hour drive from Buffalo across the United States-Canada border is Toronto, the cultural, entertainment, and financial capital of Canada. Buffalo is also ideally located for easy access to many of America's major cities. The Buffalo-Niagara International Airport offers direct flights to more than 20 cities, including New York, Boston, Philadelphia, Chicago, and Washington, DC, all only an hour's flight away.

UB has played a central role in the creation of a strong, sustainable knowledge economy and thriving entrepreneurial culture that are driving Buffalo's revitalization. Exemplified and driven by the centrally located Buffalo Niagara Medical Campus, UB's Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences, Buffalo is experiencing a period of tremendous progress and momentum as well as unprecedented regional investments in the industries of the future and in the assets that ensure a satisfying quality of life for all its citizens.

Land Acknowledgment

UB acknowledges that our campuses operate on land that is the traditional territory of the Seneca Nation, a member of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy, and the region remains the home of the Haudenosaunee people. Further, we responsibly acknowledge the continuing impact of settler colonialism on the Haudenosaunee and their territories.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Data Engineering
jobs.description:
Dropbox is a Virtual First company. For this role, we are hiring in Zones 2 and 3. Zones are determined by your zip code; if you’re within 100 miles of a listed metro area (straight-line radius), you’re included in that Zone. Please check your Zone in the Compensation section below.

Role Description

We are seeking a Senior Manager, Data Engineering to lead the team responsible for Dropbox’s underlying data foundations that power our business as a whole. This is a hands-on engineering leader who owns the pipelines and data products that Product, GTM, Finance, and the CTO organization depend on to make decisions.

In this role, you will lead and grow a team of data engineers building and operating our ingestion, transformation, orchestration, and serving layers, as well as the self-serve analytics substrate that lets partner teams answer their own questions without bespoke engineering work.

The ideal candidate is a deeply technical, product-minded engineering leader who can hold a high bar on system reliability and data quality while partnering closely with Data Science, Business Intelligence Engineering, Analytics, and Product to turn fragmented, ticket-driven data work into durable, reusable data products.

Responsibilities

Data Quality & Observability: Establish and enforce a rigorous data quality culture: lineage, freshness monitoring, anomaly detection, and outcome-oriented, gaming-resistant quality metrics.
Self-Serve Platform: Lead the engineering of the self-serve analytics substrate, reducing bespoke request volume and increasing partner-team autonomy.
Cost & Efficiency: Own the unit economics of the data platform — compute and storage efficiency — and drive measurable improvements without sacrificing reliability.
Cross-Functional Partnership: Partner deeply with Data Science, BIE, Analytics, Product, Data Platform, and the CTO org to define the semantic layer, modeling standards, and data contracts that make downstream work trustworthy and fast.
Engineering Culture: Establish rigorous engineering practices — code review, testing, CI/CD for data, incident response, and postmortems — and champion the effective, measured use of AI coding tools to improve engineering productivity.
Team Leadership: Lead, mentor, and grow a high-talent-density team of data engineers, fostering a culture of ownership, technical excellence, psychological safety, and continuous learning.

Requirements

8+ years of data engineering or backend/data infrastructure experience with increasing scope, ideally in high-scale environments.
3+ years of experience directly managing and growing engineering teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and team design.
Deep Technical Expertise: Proven track record building and operating large-scale batch and streaming pipelines (e.g., Spark, dbt, Airflow/orchestration) on a modern lakehouse or warehouse stack (e.g., Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery).
Reliability & Quality: Demonstrated ownership of data SLAs, observability, lineage, and incident response for business-critical pipelines.
Systems & Modeling: Strong data modeling fundamentals and the ability to design a semantic layer and data contracts that serve many downstream consumers.
Stakeholder Management: Excellent communication and the ability to align engineering, data science, analytics, and business partners around shared reliability and quality goals.

Preferred Qualifications

Platform / Self-Serve Experience: Track record building self-serve data or analytics platforms that reduced bespoke request volume and increased partner autonomy.
AI-Forward Engineering: Experience integrating AI coding tools and LLM-based tooling into the engineering workflow, with a measured approach to impact and guardrails.
Cost Discipline: Demonstrated success improving compute/storage unit economics without regressing reliability.
Familiarity with modern data governance, privacy, and access-control practices.
Experience operating in a pod or embedded model serving multiple business partners.

Durable Skills

Skills

AI fluency means using these tools to amplify human judgment, not replace it. We believe people with these skills will thrive as work and technology continue to evolve:

Awareness: Understand yourself and others.
Judgment: Evaluate information and make decisions in complex situations.
Adaptability: Learn, adjust, and stay effective through change.
Connection: Communicate, collaborate, and build trust.

To learn more about why these skills matter and what the data shows about thriving through change, read this blog post from our Chief People Officer, Melanie Rosenwasser.

This role is not available in Zone 1

US Zone 2
$202,700—$274,300 USD

US Zone 3

The range(s) listed above is the expected annual salary/OTE (On-Target Earnings) for this role, subject to change. Please note, OTE are for sales roles only.

Salary/OTE is just one component of Dropbox’s total rewards package. All regular employees are also eligible for the corporate bonus program or a sales incentive (target included in OTE) as well as stock in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs).

Dropbox takes a number of factors into account when determining individual starting pay, including job and level they are hired into, location/metropolitan area, skillset, and peer compensation. We target most new hire offers between the minimum up to the middle of the range.

US Zone 3: All other US locations

Company Description

Read more about our Benefits.

Dropbox isn’t just a workplace—it’s a living lab for designing a more enlightened way of working. We’re a global community of bold visionaries and resourceful doers shaping the future of Dropbox and, in turn, the future of work. Our Virtual First model combines the autonomy of a distributed workplace with the power of human connection, creating space for meaningful work and lasting relationships. With a startup mindset and enterprise-level opportunities, we expect Dropbox employees to think critically, stay curious, and use modern tools, including AI, to improve how work gets done. Here, you can be who you are and grow into who you’re meant to be. You own your impact, helping make work more intuitive, joyful, and human for yourself and hundreds of millions of people worldwide. If you’re ready to push boundaries and challenge yourself, Dropbox is ready for you.

Team Description

The Dropbox Engineering Team develops the technology, platforms, and products that create more enlightened ways of working for hundreds of millions of people. Customers rely on Dropbox to manage, share, and collaborate on content seamlessly—our engineering makes that easier and more intuitive than ever before.Our platform features a robust systems software layer that stores and processes exabytes of data, and a suite of growing services that enhance core products like our sharing and sync engine. We’re also driving innovation with new offerings such as Dash, our AI-powered knowledge management engine. Our infrastructure spans high-performance servers and cutting-edge components across multiple data centers worldwide, ensuring reliability, speed, and scalability at a global scale. We think like a startup but build for an enterprise, exploring new possibilities that transform how people work. If you're excited about turning complex technical challenges into intuitive solutions at scale, join our Engineering team.

Virtual First

Dropbox’s Virtual First way of working is designed to help people do their best work with flexibility, autonomy, and connection. Day to day, teams work remotely with nonlinear schedules and core collaboration hours that support deep focus and individual working styles. We prioritize asynchronous communication to improve clarity, respect deep work time, and reduce unnecessary meetings. While remote work is the primary experience for our employees, we also prioritize intentional, in-person connection. We bring teams together through regular team gatherings, on-demand workspaces, and Dropbox Neighborhood events in order to strengthen team cohesion, foster creativity, and enhance momentum. Virtual First is built to provide the same access to opportunity, growth, and impact for everyone, regardless of location.

This role requires travel to offsites and various other team gatherings (approximately 5-10% of the year or 2-3 days per quarter). We provide advance notice when possible and encourage candidates to discuss any accommodation needs during the interview process.

AI Fluency

AI fluency is a core part of how we work and grow. It’s not about being an expert—it’s about using these tools thoughtfully and effectively to improve your work and support others.

We Look For Four Key Behaviors In Candidates

Ownership: You use AI responsibly by protecting data, applying sound judgment, and taking accountability for the quality and accuracy of your work.
Experimentation: You explore new AI capabilities and apply them to improve workflows within approved tools and practices.
Leverage: You use AI to enhance thinking, improve efficiency, and increase your impact and your team’s.
Learning: You stay current on emerging AI tools and trends, continuously build your skills, and share what you learn with others.

Together, these behaviors help build a workforce where technology amplifies human judgment, creativity, and impact.

Dropbox supports responsible use of AI for preparation, but misrepresentation of skills or experience is not permitted. To learn more, see our approach to AI in hiring.

Dropbox is an equal opportunity employer. We are a welcoming place for everyone, and we do our best to make sure all people feel supported and connected at work.

jobs.title: Director of Production Automation and Process Engineering
jobs.description:
CI Solutions is expanding its production capacity and preparing to open a new production facility, including the addition of four to five automated UV digital printing systems.
We currently have dedicated project management, production management, and engineering resources. This role will work alongside those teams, with a specific focus on production automation, systems integration, and scaling the operation from a single production line to multiple coordinated production units.

The initial focus will be developing a complete understanding of the existing equipment and end-to-end production workflow. This leader will then define how the operation must change to support multiple production lines efficiently. They must understand the intricacies of moving from one line to many, including job routing, equipment utilization, shared resources, staffing, maintenance, quality control, production visibility, redundancy, and exception handling.

The primary objective is to build a scalable and increasingly automated production model that can sustainably reduce standard lead times from approximately 20 business days to 7–10 business days without sacrificing print quality, personalization accuracy, data integrity, or service reliability.

Key Responsibilities:

Own the strategy for scaling CI Solutions production environment from a single-line workflow to multiple coordinated production units.
Clearly articulate the business case for production investments, including expected capacity, labor impact, throughput improvement, operating risk, cost, and return.
Define how jobs should be scheduled, routed, prioritized, balanced, and reassigned across multiple production units.
Design processes that prevent equipment expansion from creating additional manual handoffs, disconnected workflows, or new production bottlenecks.
Determine which production functions should be centralized, and which should be managed at the individual line level.
Establish a scalable operating model for shared resources such as data preparation, prepress, quality control, maintenance, material handling, packaging, and shipping.
Automate data validation, personalization setup, job creation, proofing, production release, job routing, inspection, reconciliation, sorting, labeling, and reporting wherever practical.
Define the software, integration, and reporting capabilities required to manage multiple production lines.
Partner with engineering and software teams to translate production needs into clear system requirements and prioritized development work.
Lead the planning and operational launch of the new production facility.
Support the installation, commissioning, acceptance testing, and production ramp-up of 4-5 additional automated UV digital printing systems.
Validate that the facility’s electrical service, environmental controls, ventilation, networking, equipment layout, material flow, safety systems, and supporting infrastructure meet the needs of a multi-line production operation.
Develop standards for equipment configuration, calibration, UV curing, ink adhesion, color consistency, registration, white-ink applications, preventive maintenance, and changeovers.
Design the production environment for resilience so that equipment maintenance or failure does not unnecessarily stop the entire operation.
Establish measurable standards for cycle time, throughput, equipment utilization, uptime, work in progress, spoilage, rework, labor efficiency, personalization accuracy, and on-time completion.
Work closely with production management on execution while maintaining ownership of automation, process design, capacity planning, and scalable production architecture.

Required Experience:

10+ years of progressive experience in print manufacturing, production automation, process engineering, or industrial operations.
Demonstrated experience scaling an operation from one production line to multiple coordinated lines or production units.
Experience designing automated workflows that connect data intake, production equipment, quality control, and fulfillment.
Direct experience with large-format, industrial, or high-volume UV digital printing.
Ability to translate business goals and operating constraints into technical equipment, software, facility, and staffing requirements.
Experience developing capacity models and business cases for equipment, automation, and facility investments.
Experience installing, commissioning, and completing acceptance testing for new production equipment.
Strong understanding of job routing, production scheduling, line balancing, bottleneck analysis, preventive maintenance, redundancy, and process control.
Experience working across production, engineering, software, project management, and executive leadership.

Why Join CI Solutions

CI Solutions develops secure identity and credentialing solutions for schools and other organizations. For more than 30 years, we have built our business by earning the trust of our customers, partners, and employees. We value long-term relationships, approach our work with integrity, and take pride in delivering products our clients depend on every day.
We are a small, agile, and fast-paced company where employees have the opportunity to take ownership, drive meaningful improvements, collaborate across departments, and see the direct impact of their work.

Role Overview

You enjoy leading teams that ship customer-facing product experiences at scale. You bring strong front-end engineering depth, pair it with pragmatic people leadership, and love building reusable platform capabilities that help multiple product teams move faster.

In this role you’ll lead 2–3 product teams (including the core UI team), set technical direction for a micro-frontend architecture and shell SDK, and stay close to the code—especially when a problem needs hands-on help. Lead 2–3 product engineering teams (including the core UI team), providing day-to-day management, coaching, mentoring, and performance support while maintaining a strong technical presence.

8+ years of software engineering experience with 3+ years leading and managing engineers (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
Strong React 18+ expertise (hooks, Suspense, StrictMode, error boundaries, lazy loading) and modern TypeScript patterns.
Deep experience with Webpack 5 and Module Federation or similar approaches to modular front-end architecture.

Solid experience integrating or developing backend services, including API design and microservices-based architectures.

Experience with CI/CD pipelines and modern development practices including testing and code quality standards.

Strong understanding of UI architecture concepts such as design systems, theming, and responsive design.
Experience with accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1) and building inclusive user experiences.
Exposure to AI/LLM-powered UI experiences or developer productivity tools.

new_jobs.description:
Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

The Role

The Autonomous Factory Systems team builds the software that gives Hadrian's factories the ability to sense, decide, and act autonomously. This includes the core robotics stack — perception, behaviors, planning, collision avoidance, and high-level control — alongside orchestration between robots and manufacturing machines and the hardware abstraction layer that connects our software to the machines on the floor.

You will build and manage a team of engineers focused on the robotics side of this stack. This is a people-first management role: your focus is on hiring, growing, and supporting a strong team, while staying close enough to the technical work to help guide direction and staffing decisions.

What You’ll Do

Own the people leadership of your engineers: hiring, onboarding, mentorship, career growth, and performance.
Build a hiring engine for robotics talent — define the bar, run a strong interview process, and help recruit a top-tier team across perception, planning, behaviors, and control.
Ensure engineers are engaged, growing, and set up to do their best work; regularly assess team health and address issues before they become problems.
Have real input into technical direction and where we invest headcount, in close partnership with the engineers and technical leads who drive architecture and design.
Partner with Hardware, Controls, Product, and Operations to translate business priorities into a sequenced roadmap, and make sure the team is resourced and organized to deliver it.
Continuously improve the team's engineering practices and developer lifecycle: planning, design review, code review, testing, simulation, deployment, on-call, and incident response.

What We’re Looking For

5+ years of engineering management experience leading robotics, autonomy, or other complex technical teams in production.
A genuine passion for people management — you care about your engineers' growth and happiness as much as you care about what the team ships.
A track record of hiring and building strong technical teams, including for hard-to-fill or specialized roles.
Technical fluency in robotics concepts (perception, planning, behaviors, control, collision avoidance) to have informed conversations about tradeoffs, evaluate technical leads' proposals, and contribute a useful point of view on direction and prioritization — without needing to be the architect yourself.
Strong judgment on organizational design: how to structure a team, allocate headcount across projects, and balance depth vs. breadth as the stack grows.
Excellent communication and cross-functional partnership skills — you can align engineers, technical leads, hardware/controls partners, and leadership.
A track record of running a healthy team: clear expectations, direct feedback, and a strong sense of ownership among your engineers.
Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment with high stakes, physical systems, and short iteration cycles.
M.S. in Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field.

What Will Set You Apart

A track record of scaling a team through a period of fast headcount growth, including building out interview loops and onboarding from scratch.
Experience mentoring engineers to grow into broader technical leadership roles.
Experience managing engineers across multiple robotics disciplines (e.g., perception and planning)

Do you want to be part of an enterprise data solutions organization managing over 4+ petabytes of data and powering the next‑generation analytics and operational data platforms for a leading financial firm with over $10 trillion in assets under management?

At Schwab, the Operational Data Exchange (ODX) organization owns the strategy, architecture, implementation, delivery, and support of enterprise operational data platforms. Own end‑to‑end technical delivery for Contact Center operational data platforms, ensuring reliability, scalability, and alignment with evolving business priorities.

Own talent strategy for the Contact Center Data Exchange domain, including hiring, onboarding, performance management, career development, and succession planning.
Set clear expectations and goals for teams, aligning individual development plans with organizational outcomes and delivery commitments.
Build sustainable delivery capacity by strengthening leadership bench, improving execution predictability, and promoting strong team ownership across the portfolio.

What you have

Required Qualifications

15+ years of recent, hands‑on data engineering experience, with a strong focus on real-time data ingestions, APIs, and distributed systems.
5+ years of technical leadership experience, owning delivery for complex, business‑critical platforms.
5+ years of people leadership experience, leading multiple cross‑functional engineering teams.
Demonstrated experience in building scalable data ingestion frameworks to acquire and integrate data from diverse source systems in real-time, near real-time, and batch modes into operational data stores and enterprise data warehouses for downstream consumption.
Strong understanding of data modeling and storage strategies optimized for both operational and analytical use cases, including designing data structures that support reporting, low-latency access, and high-performance analytics.
Hands-on experience leveraging AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Copilot or similar) to accelerate engineering productivity, automate code generation and testing, and drive measurable improvements in developer efficiency and delivery timelines.
Deep expertise with Java, Spring (Boot/Batch), REST APIs, Microservices, and SQL.
Strong public cloud experience (3+ years), with preference for GCP and cloud‑native architecture patterns.
Hands‑on experience with streaming technologies such as Kafka, Pub/Sub, Kinesis, or RabbitMQ.
Proven experience leading large‑scale data platform migrations or modernization initiatives.
Strong CI/CD experience using tools such as GitHub, Jenkins, Bamboo, Bitbucket, and automated testing frameworks.
Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with senior leadership, including presenting technical strategies, risks, and outcomes to non‑technical audiences.
Recent hands‑on experience is required—this role is expected to actively engage in design, troubleshooting, and critical technical decisions.
Demonstrated success building and scaling high‑performing engineering organizations with strong retention and engagement.

Preferred Qualifications

Contact Center domain experience, particularly within a data organization, supporting platforms such as NICE, Cresta, or similar ecosystems.
Experience supporting AI‑enabled operational use cases, real‑time analytics, or intelligent routing systems.
Experience with Operational Data Stores / Exchanges, enterprise data integration, and high‑availability data platforms.
Working knowledge of data warehousing concepts, Informatica IDMC / Power Center, or similar ETL technologies.
Prior experience serving as a technical lead for distributed, cross‑geography teams.

What’s in it for you

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. We champion your growth through meaningful work, continuous learning, and a culture of trust and collaboration—so you can build the skills to make a lasting impact. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan

Paid parental leave and family building benefits
Tuition reimbursement
Health, dental, and vision insurance

This is a career-defining opportunity for a technology leader who has built AI-native engineering cultures, delivered AI-powered platforms in complex regulated industries, and knows how to win in both the automotive and insurance environments.

The Head of Software Engineering owns software engineering strategy and execution across Safe-Guard's core platform portfolio. You will lead a multi-team engineering organization that builds and operates the systems underpinning dealer enrollment, incentive programs, rating, quoting, and remitting workflows, claims adjudication, cancellations, payment processing, and direct-to-consumer product experiences. Engineering Leadership & Team Development

Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing software engineering organization across multiple product domains, client-facing dealer and OEM platforms, internal operations systems, and direct-to-consumer applications.
Own recruiting, hiring, and retention of top engineering talent; build career progression that reward technical excellence and leadership growth at every level.
Establish and sustain a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous learning for engineers do their best work.
Conduct regular 1:1s, performance reviews, and career development conversations; actively develop direct reports into future leaders.
Partner with HR and Talent Acquisition to strengthen Safe-Guard's employer brand within the software engineering community.

Platform Ownership & Technical Strategy

Own the engineering roadmap and outcomes for Safe-Guard's client-facing platforms (dealer enrollment, rating, quoting, contract remittance, incentive management, direct-to-consumer) and internal platforms (claims adjudication, cancellations, and payments).
Define and help drive the technical architecture strategy, balancing modernization, and scalability, across a portfolio of applications serving automotive and insurance workflows.
Partner with Sales, Product Management, and Operations to translate business objectives into executable technical roadmaps, ensuring alignment between engineering capacity and company priorities.
Drive continuous improvement in system reliability, performance, and security; establish engineering standards for code quality, testing, observability, and incident response.
Make sound architectural and build/buy/partner decisions, clearly communicating trade-offs to senior leadership and stakeholders.

AI-Native Culture & Platform Development

Help champion Safe-Guard's AI vision by embedding AI-assisted development practices as standard practice across all engineering teams.
In collaboration with technology leadership, help design and delivery of AI-native platform capabilities, including intelligent automation in claims adjudication, contract processing, rating workflows, and dealer-facing experiences.
Build a team culture where engineers default to AI-first thinking: leveraging AI to accelerate development velocity, improve code quality, reduce operational work, and expand product capabilities.
Stay current on AI tooling and agentic AI approaches; bring informed recommendations to the technology and product leadership on emerging capabilities applicable to Safe-Guard's platforms.

Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

As a Senior Engineering Manager, Communications, you'll lead the team responsible for in-game text chat — one of the most-used surfaces on Roblox and a cornerstone of how our community connects. Every day this system carries billions of messages across hundreds of millions of users, in real time, across 2D and 3D spaces, on every device we support. You'll own the roadmap and the engineering org behind it: building rich, immersive, and engaging communication experiences that let people and creators express themselves safely and seamlessly — better than in real life.

This is a role for a leader who thinks like a product builder as much as an engineer. You'll balance the demands of massive scale and rock-solid reliability with a relentless focus on the user experience, shipping features that make conversation on Roblox feel effortless, expressive, and safe. You'll grow and develop a team of engineers, set technical direction, and partner deeply across product, design, trust & safety, and infrastructure to define what communication on Roblox becomes next.

You Will

Lead, grow, and develop a team of software engineers building the in-game text chat platform, setting a high bar for engineering excellence, ownership, and career growth.
Own the technical vision and multi-quarter roadmap for real-time text messaging, balancing new product capabilities against scale, latency, reliability, and cost.
Drive the architecture and evolution of messaging systems that reliably deliver billions of messages per day at low latency to a global, cross-platform audience.
Partner with product and design to shape a compelling communication experience — treating chat as a product, not just infrastructure — and translate ambiguous goals into concrete plans and shipped features.
Collaborate closely with Trust & Safety, Policy, and ML teams to ensure every messaging experience is safe and civil by design for a young, global user base.
Establish strong engineering practices around quality, observability, on-call health, and operational excellence for systems that must always be available.
Communicate clearly and influence across the organization — with peers, leadership, and cross-functional partners — to align teams behind a shared direction.

You Have

8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years managing and growing engineering teams.
A track record of building and shipping consumer-facing products at scale — ideally messaging, communications, social, or other real-time systems.
Strong product intuition: you make thoughtful tradeoffs between user experience, technical complexity, and speed, and you care about what you ship, not just how it's built.
Deep experience designing and operating large-scale distributed systems, with a strong grasp of reliability, latency, and the realities of running high-throughput services in production.
Demonstrated ability to attract, develop, and retain strong engineers, and to build healthy, high-performing teams.
Excellent communication and cross-functional leadership skills, with a history of driving alignment across product, design, and engineering.

new_jobs.title: Director of Software Engineering
new_jobs.description:
Director, Software Engineering
Position Overview

We are seeking an accomplished Director of Software Engineering
to provide strategic and technical leadership for the development of sophisticated, mission-critical software supporting advanced industrial, manufacturing, and defense-related programs.

This senior leadership role will be responsible for establishing the software engineering vision, shaping technical direction, and overseeing the delivery of secure, dependable, and high-performance software platforms. The Director will work across engineering, product development, systems engineering, manufacturing, quality, cybersecurity, and program management organizations to ensure software capabilities support both current operational requirements and long-term business objectives.

The successful candidate will bring a combination of deep software engineering expertise, organizational leadership, architectural judgment, and experience delivering complex systems in highly regulated or technically demanding environments.

Key Responsibilities
Establish and execute a long-term software engineering strategy aligned with organizational objectives, product roadmaps, and evolving technology requirements.
Provide technical direction across multiple software development programs and ensure consistent engineering practices across teams.
Lead the architecture, design, development, integration, verification, deployment, and sustainment of mission-critical software.
Oversee engineering organizations responsible for embedded, application, platform, systems, and other software technologies as appropriate.
Work closely with product and systems engineering leadership to translate customer and operational requirements into scalable software solutions.
Partner with manufacturing and operations teams to ensure software development activities effectively support production, integration, testing, and lifecycle requirements.
Establish appropriate architectural standards, development methodologies, coding practices, and engineering processes.
Champion modern software development approaches, including automation, continuous integration and delivery, DevSecOps, automated testing, and disciplined configuration management.
Promote appropriate adoption of cloud, data, artificial intelligence, automation, and other emerging technologies where they provide meaningful business or technical value.
Ensure software solutions meet applicable requirements for security, reliability, safety, quality, maintainability, and regulatory compliance.
Collaborate with cybersecurity and information assurance teams to incorporate security throughout the software development lifecycle rather than treating it as a final-stage activity.
Establish engineering metrics and performance indicators to monitor delivery, quality, reliability, technical debt, productivity, and operational effectiveness.
Identify technical risks and organizational constraints and develop strategies to address them before they affect program execution.
Balance near-term delivery commitments with longer-term investments in architecture, infrastructure, tooling, modernization, and engineering capability.
Provide technical guidance during major design reviews, architecture decisions, program planning activities, and critical issue resolution.
Ensure engineering teams maintain appropriate documentation, development standards, test strategies, and configuration controls.
Support the evaluation and introduction of new technologies, tools, platforms, and development methodologies.
Coordinate software development activities across geographically distributed teams and ensure effective collaboration between locations and functions.

Organizational Leadership
A major component of this position is building and developing a strong engineering organization.
The Director will:
Lead and mentor engineering managers and senior technical leaders.
Establish clear organizational structures, responsibilities, objectives, and performance expectations.
Recruit, develop, and retain highly skilled software engineering professionals.
Build succession plans and create opportunities for technical and leadership development.
Foster an environment where engineers are encouraged to challenge assumptions, propose improvements, and take ownership of technical outcomes.
Promote collaboration between software, systems, hardware, manufacturing, product, quality, and cybersecurity organizations.
Develop a culture centered on accountability, engineering excellence, continuous learning, and measurable improvement.
Encourage knowledge sharing and consistency of engineering practices across teams and locations.
Help create an inclusive environment in which diverse technical perspectives contribute to better engineering decisions.

Program & Product Partnership
The Director will serve as a senior software representative in broader product and program discussions. This includes partnering with stakeholders to establish realistic development strategies, prioritize technical investments, and align engineering capacity with business needs.
You will help ensure that software roadmaps remain synchronized with product development, system architecture, manufacturing schedules, customer requirements, and future technology initiatives.

The role will also involve communicating complex technical issues to senior leadership, clearly explaining tradeoffs, risks, resource requirements, and recommended courses of action.

Quality, Safety & Security
Because the software supports high-consequence applications, strong attention to reliability and compliance is essential.

The Director will help ensure that engineering teams:
Apply appropriate software quality and verification practices.
Incorporate cybersecurity principles throughout development and deployment.
Follow applicable safety, regulatory, contractual, and industry requirements.
Maintain rigorous configuration and change-control processes.
Identify and mitigate reliability and security risks.
Establish appropriate automated and manual testing strategies.
Address defects and technical debt systematically.
Maintain traceability between requirements, implementation, verification, and released capabilities.
Continuously improve engineering processes based on lessons learned and measurable performance data.

Strategic Technology Leadership
Beyond day-to-day delivery, this position will help define the organization's future software capabilities.

The Director will evaluate emerging technologies and determine where modernization can improve engineering efficiency, product capability, scalability, security, or competitiveness. This may include evaluating new development frameworks, automation platforms, AI-assisted engineering tools, distributed architectures, advanced simulation environments, data platforms, or other technologies relevant to the organization's products.

The ideal leader will understand that modernization is not simply about adopting new technology; it requires thoughtful architecture, disciplined implementation, effective change management, and measurable business or engineering outcomes.

What We're Looking For
The ideal candidate is a strategic engineering leader who remains technically credible while operating effectively at an organizational level. You should be comfortable moving between high-level strategy and detailed technical discussions and have demonstrated success leading complex software organizations.

Strong candidates will typically bring:
Significant experience leading software engineering organizations.
A strong background in software architecture, development, integration, and delivery.
Experience managing engineering managers and senior technical professionals.
Demonstrated success delivering complex, high-reliability or mission-critical software.
Experience working in environments where security, safety, quality, and regulatory requirements are important.
Strong understanding of modern software engineering practices and development methodologies.
Experience establishing technical strategy and multi-year engineering roadmaps.
Strong program and stakeholder management capabilities.
Excellent written, verbal, and executive communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop, and retain high-performing technical teams.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
The ability to make sound technical decisions while balancing schedule, cost, risk, quality, and long-term maintainability.

Leadership Profile

We are looking for a leader who can combine technical depth with organizational vision
. The successful candidate will be able to establish direction without unnecessarily restricting innovation, create accountability without compromising collaboration, and make difficult engineering decisions while keeping teams focused on mission and customer outcomes.

This is an opportunity to influence the technology strategy of a sophisticated organization, shape the next generation of software capabilities, and build an engineering culture capable of delivering dependable solutions for some of the most technically challenging applications in the industry.

new_jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Machine Learning
new_jobs.description:
About Checkr

Checkr is building the data platform to power safe and fair decisions. Over 140,000 companies and millions of people rely on Checkr for AI verification in the moments that matter most: getting a new job, a new place to live, a car ride, childcare, even a date. Customers include Uber, Pennymac, Airbnb, Doordash, and Anthropic.

We’re a team that thrives on solving complex problems with innovative solutions that advance our mission. Checkr is recognized on Forbes Cloud 100 2025 List and is a Y Combinator 2024 Breakthrough Company.

We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to lead the Machine Learning Engineering team inside Checkr’s Data & ML organization. This team sits at the heart of our product's strategic advantage, making millions of background checks faster, more accurate, and more trustworthy.

The Team Owns Three Connected Areas

Core product intelligence: NLP and classification systems, entity resolution, profile integrity, model accuracy, and the production services that power Checkr’s products.
Workforce integrity: resume and identity fraud, multi-signal risk detection, and new products that help customers identify sophisticated hiring fraud
ML and agent infrastructure: evaluation systems, observability, model lifecycle, agent orchestration, and reusable infrastructure that helps every team ship reliable AI faster.

This is an engineering leadership role, not a research-management role: you will lead ML engineers across seniority levels, stay close enough to the work to set technical direction, and hold the team accountable for production outcomes. You will decide where ML should continue to create a strategic advantage for Checkr.

You will also shape Checkr’s broader AI strategy. The near-term agenda includes building a measurable accuracy moat in our core products, launching an end-to-end workforce-integrity product, and creating the evaluation and knowledge infrastructure required to operate AI agents in a regulated domain. This role reports to the Sr. Director of Data & ML within Engineering. This role is based in San Francisco. We are looking for someone who is seeking less process and more shipping, less paperwork and more results.

What You’ll Do

Lead and grow the ML Engineering team. Hire, coach, and develop ML engineers. Set clear ownership, grow technical leaders, and build a team that generates its own roadmap.
Set the strategy and roadmap. Turn ambiguous company priorities into a focused, multi-quarter ML agenda. Put investment on work that improves customer outcomes, revenue, accuracy, reliability, or cost. Stop work that does not.
Raise the production engineering bar. Models and agents ship as dependable software: clear APIs, tests, CI/CD, observability, on-call ownership, and defined reliability targets.
Build the ML operating model. Establish shared approaches to evaluation, golden sets, training-data provenance, model and prompt versioning, monitoring, retraining, latency, and cost. Replace artisanal evaluation with repeatable systems.
Advance core product intelligence. Guide systems for classification, information extraction, entity resolution, profile integrity, and accuracy. Make model quality measurable in production and drive the feedback loops that improve it.
Launch new AI and fraud products. Partner with Product, Security, Operations, and go-to-market teams to turn signals across identity, resume, device, and employment data into customer products.
Lead Checkr’s agentic transition. Guide the design of AI systems that combine specialized models, LLMs, tools, and governed knowledge.
Operate as an executive partner. Explain technical choices and risks in plain language. Align Product Engineering, Product, Operations, Legal, Security, and company leadership when incentives or constraints conflict.
Model AI-native leadership. Use AI to increase the team’s speed and ambition. Keep ownership of every output. As generated code becomes cheaper, raise the bar on judgment, verification, and system design.

What You Bring

10+ years building software and machine learning or AI systems, with a clear progression in scope and impact.
3+ years managing ML or software engineers, including hiring and developing senior and staff-level technical leaders.
A strong software-engineering foundation and a record of shipping ML systems that run in production.
Technical depth across the ML lifecycle: data and labeling, experimentation, model selection, deployment, APIs, CI/CD, observability, evaluation, retraining, and incident response.
Sound judgment across classical ML, deep learning, LLMs, rules, and conventional software.
Experience setting direction for NLP, classification, extraction, entity resolution, risk, fraud, recommendation, or similarly complex applied-ML domains.
Fluency with modern LLM systems, including structured outputs, tool use, agent orchestration, retrieval, evaluation, latency, quality, and cost trade-offs.
A record of translating an ambiguous business problem into a sharp roadmap, measurable outcomes, and shipped systems.
Strong people leadership. You create leverage through clear ownership, candid feedback, delegation, and coaching.
Executive-level communication and cross-functional influence. You can make a hard technical trade-off legible to senior leaders and leave the room with a decision.
You use modern AI tools to move faster, verify their output, and can spot plausible-looking work that should not ship.
An A-player mindset with a strong bias for action: you raise the bar, move with urgency, stay resilient through ambiguity, and take ownership to deliver meaningful outcomes.

Nice to have

Built ML infrastructure or MLOps platforms used by multiple teams.
Document intelligence, OCR, graph systems, identity resolution, trust and safety, fraud, or risk.
Operated ML in a compliance-sensitive domain such as fintech, legal tech, HR tech, healthcare, or security.
Python, AWS/SageMaker or similar cloud ML platforms, Snowflake, Spark, and modern data tooling.
Launched a new AI product from early customer discovery through production scale.

At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.

At Lilly, Synthetic Molecule Design and Development (SMDD) is involved in key activities for the development of synthetic active pharmaceutical ingredients from pre-clinical phases through commercialization of drug substances and drug products. Our scientists and engineers develop key technical and business solutions across the portfolio using their deep technical expertise to accelerate testing of the clinical hypothesis and overall drug development. SMDD delivers on these responsibilities by recognizing diverse talent and cultures are necessary to bring the next generation of life changing medicines to patients.

Position Summary

Our team is looking for experienced, creative, and energetic candidates to lead unit operation development and process optimization of synthetic drug candidates to support clinical trials, regulatory submission, and product commercialization. Responsibilities

Possess fluent knowledge in unit operation design, process modeling, process equipment selection, and scale-up methodologies with a drive to challenge existing methods; create and apply cutting edge technology and novel platforms within a time constrained environment.
Familiarity and working knowledge of modern synthetic organic chemistry.

Ph.D. in chemical engineering or a closely related field with 8+ years of experience; or MS degree with 15+ years of experience.

Experience with technical transfer of processes into manufacturing operations required

Prior experience in the development of an active ingredient and associated formulated product is acceptable. Relevant industrial sectors include agrochemicals, nutraceuticals, specialty chemicals, and personal care products.

Additional Skills/Preferences

Experience with authoring regulatory submissions and responding to regulatory questions.
Experience with modeling and simulation tools, data analytics, and predictive analytics.
Experience with online and offline analytical techniques and process analytical technologies (PAT).
Strong technical skills to supply business value.
Creativity and ability to transform ideas into marketable products and processes.
Knowledge and experience with management of a technical project.
Demonstrated leadership capabilities especially in a team environment.
Demonstrated ability to drive and accept change.
Demonstrated success in persuasion, influence and negotiation.
Good interpersonal skills and a sustained tendency for collaboration.
Ability to prioritize multiple activities and manage ambiguity.
Ability to influence others to promote a positive work environment.
Understanding and awareness of the external scientific and regulatory landscape.
Demonstrated initiative and risk-taking.
Demonstrated technical proficiency and ability to create ideas for future work plans.
Established external publication record.

new_jobs.title: Wastewater Director of Engineering (Mid-Atlantic)
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Veolia in North America is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country's largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. Veolia helps commercial, industrial, healthcare, higher education and municipality customers throughout North America. Headquartered in Boston, Veolia has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across North America.

Job Description

Position Purpose:

This position is responsible for directing all activities related to the management of the Mid-Atlantic Engineering Department for the successful delivery of the overall capital plan for the region. Projects will include Water and Wastewater Projects, including water treatment upgrades, pump stations, storage tanks, pipelines, and other facilities, and wastewater upgrades related to wastewater plants, lift stations and the collection system.

The candidate works closely with Engineering and Operations personnel, managing and coordinating program activities utilizing a cross functional team approach.

The candidate works with a variety of internal and external stakeholders to ensure the capital plan is developed and delivered to meet the system needs, while working with Regulators on compliance and rate filing activities, and being part of a Team to implement the Company's strategic growth plan.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities

Accountable for delivery of $50M+ of water/wastewater projects annually, including conceptual design/development, coordination of pilot testing, development of the project plans and project delivery through closeout.
Responsible for hiring, supervising, managing, mentoring the Engineering Team.
Works closely with the rate department to develop capital plans and testimony for rate filings as well as testifying before rate commissions as needed.
Support or lead business development efforts and participate in external professional activities that enhance Veolia's standing with state, regional, and national environmental and economic regulators.
Ensure corporate Technical and Environmental Health and Safety/Security standards are incorporated into the design specifications of projects.
Manage environmental and governmental permitting in coordination with local business unit staff.
Support the oversight of construction management personnel to ensure timely completion of assignments, budget compliance and adherence to applicable standards.
Drive efficiency into project delivery through the monitoring of delivery metrics and utilization of alternate procurement and delivery methods.
Provide monthly reports to management regarding the status of capital projects and issues affecting project performance.
Participate in the development of engineering design and delivery processes and standards.
Provide technical expertise on engineering and operational issues and support facility condition assessments for water/wastewater operations.
Ability to work transversally with corporate and local business units.

Work Environment

Successful candidates must be willing to travel to the various business unit sites as per job requirements.
Job sites generally located within a 30-mile radius of the local office with the occasional requirement for sites that are a longer distance.
The Director of Engineering for the Mid-Atlantic region will be based in either Wilmington, DE or Harrisburg, PA, with regular presence required at both office locations.

Qualifications

Education/Experience/Background:

Bachelor's Degree in Civil, Mechanical or Environmental Engineering.
Minimum 15 years of experience managing water/wastewater design and construction projects and upgrade projects for treatment plants, pumping stations, wastewater collection systems and water transmission/distribution systems.
5+ year Experience leading and managing multi-faceted teams.
Experience utilizing alternate project delivery methods (design-build, integrated project delivery) and contracting methods (guaranteed maximum price, reimbursable).

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

Thorough working knowledge of water and wastewater processes and system development.
Superior personal effectiveness skills, visible "leadership by example" utilizing participative management involving employees and teamwork whenever possible.
Strong project management skills (initiating, planning, executing, monitoring, controlling and closing).
Strong communication, presentation and reporting skills.
Computer skills (MS Project, Google Suite, Oracle PeopleSoft, Oracle Hyperion or other planning/performance/budgeting tools a plus).
Financial analysis skills, including budget management, ongoing assessment of project risks/opportunities and basic accounting knowledge.

Required Certification/Licenses/Training

Professional Engineer License (PE) required.
PMP and/or Construction Management certifications a plus.

Additional Information

Benefits:
Veolia's comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. In addition, employees are also entitled to participate in an employer sponsored 401(k) plan, to save for retirement. Pay and benefits for employees represented by a union are outlined in their collective bargaining agreement.

new_jobs.title: Director, Engineering - Substation
new_jobs.description:
About Us

QISG leverages Quanta’s comprehensive resources to deliver collaborative solutions for our partners' energy infrastructure needs. We use in-house talent, expertise and resources to plan, design, engineer, manage, conduct maintenance on and construct projects.

Our turnkey service capabilities provide our customers with efficiency, consistency, attention to detail and safe execution. The QISG team brings together Engineering, Safety, Quality, Material Procurement, QA/QC, Right-of-Way Acquisition, Scheduling, Environmental Planning, Permitting, Title and Land Management expertise that ensure outstanding results for our clients.

About This Role

JOB TITLE:
Director, Engineering

The Director of Engineering for Substation is a senior leadership role responsible for overseeing the planning, design, and implementation of Substation projects. This role involves managing a team of engineers and technical staff, ensuring that projects meet regulatory, safety, and quality standards, and supporting the company's strategic objectives. The Director will collaborate with other departments, stakeholders, and external partners to drive innovation, efficiency, and operational excellence in the company's transmission and substation engineering activities.

What You'll Do

Lead, mentor, and develop a team of engineers and technical professionals.
Establish and maintain a high-performance culture, with a focus on continuous improvement and innovation.
Foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment that values diverse perspectives and talents.
Oversee the planning, design, and execution of transmission and substation projects, ensuring alignment with company goals and regulatory requirements.
Develop project budgets, schedules, and resource plans, and ensure projects are delivered on time and within budget.
Manage risks and resolve issues that may impact project scope, quality, and delivery.
Provide technical guidance and expertise in the design and optimization of transmission and substation systems.
Stay current with industry trends, technologies, and regulatory changes, and integrate best practices into the engineering processes.
Ensure compliance with safety, environmental, and regulatory standards in all engineering activities.
Contribute to the development of the company's strategic plans and objectives, particularly in the areas of transmission and substation infrastructure.
Identify and evaluate new business opportunities, partnerships, and technologies that can enhance the company's competitive position.
Collaborate with other departments, such as Operations, Finance, and Regulatory Affairs, to align engineering initiatives with broader business goals.
Build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including customers, regulators, contractors, and suppliers.
Represent the company at industry forums, conferences, and regulatory meetings, advocating for the company's interests and promoting its capabilities.

What You'll Bring

Minimum of 15 years’ experience in the electric utility industry performing engineering related duties and/or management for high voltage electrical projects.
Bachelor of Science degree (B.S.) or Graduate degree in Electrical Engineering from an ABET accredited university.
P.E. license required.
Proven track record of successfully leading multidisciplinary engineering teams and delivering complex projects on time and within budget.
Strong technical expertise in structural, civil, electrical, or mechanical engineering, with a comprehensive understanding of engineering principles and practices.
Expert knowledge of electric utility engineering and construction standards.
Advanced knowledge of utility industry processes including scheduling, contracts, coordinating and managing all disciplines.
Excellent business acumen and experience managing departmental budgets.
Knowledge of process and procedures for project controls and estimates.
Experience interpreting internal and external business issues, recommending best practices, mitigating risk and solving complex problems.
Demonstrated experience supporting external customers.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and leadership skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with internal teams, clients, and external partners.
Demonstrated ability to develop and execute strategic plans, drive innovation, and achieve business objectives.
Knowledge of relevant industry codes, standards, and regulations, including ANSI, ASTM, ACI, AISC, NEC, NESC, and others.
Able to deal with ambiguity and ability to work independently, manage multiple tasks and determine priorities in a complex environment.

What You'll Get

Competitive Compensation
401(k) Retirement Plan
Holiday Pay
Paid Time Off (PTO)
Comprehensive Health Coverage
Pet Insurance
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Professional Development
Tuition Assistance
Employee Discount Program

The Product Line Director (PLD) for the AV EW Communications Technology group is responsible for overall product line ownership, assists with management of production programs, assists with program execution, and lifecycle management across the AV EW Communications Technology portfolio. This role serves as the business and execution lead for AV EW Communications Technology programs, partnering closely with the AV EW leadership, chief engineering team and business development team to drive the technical roadmap while ensuring disciplined execution from concept development through production, fielding, and sustainment.

The PLD is responsible for program performance, cost, schedule, risk, and customer satisfaction, and acts as the primary interface between customers, AV EW senior leadership and chief engineering team. This position plays a critical role in scaling EW System capabilities into operational Communications Technology for U.S. Government customers.

Key Responsibilities

Product Line & Program Leadership:

Responsible for end-to-end execution of the AV EW Communications Technology product line across all phases of the program lifecycle: capture, development, integration, production, fielding, and sustainment
For programs associated with the AV EW Communications Technology group the PLD is responsible for cost, schedule, technical performance, and delivery commitments
Partner with the AV EW leadership and chief engineering team to align technical roadmap, architecture decisions, and capability evolution with customer requirements and business strategy
Lead cross-functional integrated product teams (IPTs) including engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, contracts, and finance

Develop, manage, and execute program budgets, EACs, forecasts, and margin performance
Ensure disciplined program controls, risk management, and change management across contracts
Drive affordability, scalability, and producibility initiatives aligned with customer acquisition strategies
Support pricing strategies, proposal development, and negotiation for new programs, follow-ons, and production options

Customer & Stakeholder Engagement

Act as a senior customer interface for AV EW Communications Technology programs with U.S. Army, NNSA, U.S. Air Force, and other DoD and interagency stakeholders
Support customer engagements including design reviews, program reviews, test events, fielding activities, and operational demonstrations
Translate evolving customer CONOPS and mission needs into executable program plans and product enhancements
Represent the AV EW Communications Technology product line in internal and external executive-level forums

Execution, Production & Sustainment

Oversee sustainment planning, field support, spares, upgrades, and lifecycle cost reduction efforts

Support deployed Communications Technology with responsiveness and operational urgency

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Physics, Business, or a related field (advanced degree preferred)
10+ years of experience in defense programs, product line management, or program management
Demonstrated experience leading directed energy, advanced weapons, or complex defense Communications Technology
Strong working knowledge of EACs, program financials, earned value concepts, and execution metrics
Experience working directly with U.S. Army, NNSA, U.S. Air Force, and/or other government customers
Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams delivering complex, mission-critical Communications Technology

Ability to obtain TS/SCI clearance

Secret

$148,000 - $237,000

We’re looking for a Director, Enterprise AI & Platform Engineering to lead high-impact AI, automation, and platform initiatives that help teams work smarter and build faster.
